title: Mechanism-driven artificial intelligence for food cold-chain control and governance
abstract: Background Food cold chains are critical infrastructures for safeguarding perishable foods, yet prevailing management strategies remain largely rule-based, relying on sparse environmental monitoring, conservative safety margins and endpoint inspection. Such approaches insufficiently capture product-level micro-environment variability and deterioration kinetics, resulting in recurrent temperature abuse, avoidable food loss, excessive energy consumption and elevated greenhouse-gas emissions. Scope and approach This review advances a mechanism-driven perspective on artificial intelligence (AI) in food cold-chain systems. Rather than treating AI as a generic optimisation tool, we examine how near-product, multimodal sensing can be coupled with kinetics-informed and physics-aware models to infer remaining shelf life, safety margins and quality risk in real time. We synthesise evidence on how these mechanism-linked outputs inform dynamic process control, quality-based logistics allocation, first-expired–first-out implementation and energy-aware operation. Particular emphasis is placed on model interpretability, uncertainty quantification, external validation and clearly defined applicability domains as prerequisites for trustworthy deployment. Key findings and conclusions Across reported studies, AI demonstrates tangible value only when tightly anchored to measurable micro-environments and explicit deterioration mechanisms, and when embedded within governed decision loops aligned with formal food-safety management systems. We distil core design principles for mechanism-driven cold-chain intelligence: robust sensing and calibration; physics-informed feature construction; uncertainty-aware modelling; transparent validation across products and scenarios; and controlled transferability. Under these conditions, AI-enabled systems can transition cold chains from static compliance frameworks to dynamic, risk-based governance structures, with realistic potential to reduce avoidable losses, optimise energy demand and lower emissions while enhancing transparency and accountability in cold-chain performance.

title: Taste peptides: A critical review on taste perception mechanisms, AI-driven screening, and multidimensional evaluation technologies

verified_metadata.abstract: Taste peptides are a class of bioactive peptides that enhance flavor and significantly improve the palatability and overall taste profile of foods. Owing to their unique sensory properties and potential nutritional benefits, taste peptides have become a focal research area in food science and industrial applications. However, conventional screening and evaluation methods suffer from limitations such as low efficiency and long development cycles. The integration of artificial intelligence with biosensing technologies offers a novel paradigm for intelligent screening and mechanistic elucidation of taste peptides. This review summarizes the molecular perception mechanisms, structure-activity relationships, and current preparation and identification technologies of taste peptides. It critically highlights the application of deep learning in the high-throughput screening of taste peptides and systematically outlines methods, including electroencephalography, for evaluating taste intensity and elucidating taste mechanisms. Deep learning demonstrates exceptional predictive performance in the high-throughput screening of taste peptides. Furthermore, techniques such as electroencephalography and bioelectronic tongues have been validated as effective tools for quantifying gustatory responses. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations provide powerful tools to unravel the interactions between taste peptides and taste receptors. This review offers theoretical foundations and technical pathways for the rational design, intelligent screening, and industrial application of taste peptides in functional seasonings and health-promoting foods.

title: Integrating ionic liquids and artificial intelligence for circular agri-food waste valorization
abstract: Background Agri-food waste is a major environmental burden but also a rich source of polyphenols, proteins, polysaccharides, and fibers. Conventional extraction methods often suffer from low selectivity, degradation of sensitive compounds, and high energy demand. Ionic liquids (ILs), with tunable structures, negligible volatility, and strong solvating capacity, have emerged as promising solvents for valorizing these residues. Scope and approach This review summarizes the key mechanisms underlying IL-assisted extraction, including hydrogen bonding, π-π stacking, hydrophobic/hydrophilic interactions, electrostatic interactions, and biomass disruption at the macro scale. It also examines process-intensified IL systems, such as ultrasound-, microwave-, enzymatic-, and aqueous two-phase-assisted extraction, which have achieved reported yield improvements of about 1.2- to 5.4-fold over conventional methods. In parallel, artificial intelligence (AI) tools, including machine learning, deep learning, Bayesian optimization, and generative models, are discussed as emerging approaches for IL screening, property prediction, and process optimization. Key findings and conclusions Integrating ILs with AI can shift IL-assisted extraction from empirical trial-and-error toward predictive solvent screening and process optimization, improving extraction efficiency, selectivity, and bioactive stability. However, AI should be viewed as a screening and decision-support tool rather than a direct solution to the intrinsic cost, recovery, toxicity, regulatory, and scale-up barriers of IL-based systems. Future development should integrate AI-assisted optimization with experimental validation, solvent-recycling studies, techno-economic analysis, life cycle assessment, and safety/regulatory evaluation to assess the realistic industrial potential of IL-assisted agri-food waste valorization.

verified_metadata.abstract:
Background
Protein nanofibrils (PNFs) derived from oil crop bio-products are emerging as sustainable biomaterials for food and pharmaceutics. However, due to the complex process-structure-function relationship, their controllable manufacturing, precise structural regulation and functional prediction are still challenging.
Scope and approach
This review systematically outlines the preparation, characterization, properties, and applications of oil crop-derived PNFs (ODPNFs). Moving beyond conventional summaries, it critically addresses key bottlenecks, including the lack of precise structural control, difficulties in functionality prediction, and the limited understanding of structure–function relationships governing their performance. We propose a paradigm shift toward a data-driven research framework leveraging artificial intelligence (AI).
Key findings and conclusions
The potential of AI in rationalizing ODPNFs design, predicting function, and modeling nanofibril assembly behavior, structure-function relationship, and gastrointestinal performance was explored. We synthesize recent breakthroughs in AI for protein design, process optimization, structural analysis, and bioactivity prediction, evaluating their translational potential for ODPNFs. Finally, we envision an integrated future where AI orchestrates multi-omics data and automated experimentation to accelerate the on-demand design, safety evaluation, and high-value utilization of ODPNFs, thereby providing a novel perspective for advancing this field.

title: Authentication of flours using chromatographic and spectroscopic techniques: A comprehensive review
abstract: ABSTRACT Background Flour is a powdered substance obtained by grinding cereal grains or other starch-rich foods, formed through a milling process that reduces the grain to a fine powder. Flour is a staple ingredient highly susceptible to adulteration, mislabelling, and cross-contamination, posing risks to food safety, quality, and consumer trust. The increasing complexity of flour matrices and supply chains has intensified the need for reliable analytical tools for authentication. Scope and approach This review systematically evaluates recent advances in chromatographic and spectroscopic techniques for flour authentication, covering studies from 2015–2025 (chromatography) and 2020–2025 (spectroscopy). Both targeted and non-targeted approaches are discussed, including GC, LC, and CE, as well as NIR, FTIR, hyperspectral imaging, fluorescence, Raman, and LIBS. Particular attention is given to chemometric and machine learning strategies for classification and quantification, alongside key methodological considerations such as sample preparation, data processing, and validation. Key findings and conclusions Chromatographic methods provide high sensitivity and molecular specificity, enabling targeted detection of markers, while spectroscopic techniques offer rapid, non-destructive, and high-throughput screening based on chemical fingerprints. Despite significant progress, major challenges remain, including matrix complexity, environmental variability, limited standardization, and poor model transferability across instruments and datasets. Detection of low-level adulteration in complex or blended flours remains particularly challenging. Future research is expected to focus on multi-sensor data fusion, expansion of open spectral databases, robust validation frameworks, and integration of portable devices with digital infrastructures. These developments will be essential to improve robustness, scalability, and real-world implementation of flour authentication strategies.

title: Applications of artificial intelligence in toxicity prediction of food-derived functional peptides: Recent advances and future perspectives

ai4s_review.rationale: 综述食品功能肽毒性预测的序列、结构图和多模态模型，讨论数据构建、验证与安全性评价。

verified_metadata.abstract:
Background
Food-derived functional peptides have attracted increasing attention for their potential in nutritional regulation, flavor formation, and health promotion, but potential toxicity may arise during protein release, processing, gastrointestinal digestion, and dietary exposure. Conventional in vitro and in vivo assays provide essential safety evidence, yet they are often costly and time-consuming. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers a high-throughput strategy for preliminary risk screening, toxicity prediction, and prioritization of experimental validation.
Scope and approach
This review summarizes recent progress in AI-assisted toxicity prediction of food-derived peptides. It outlines conventional toxicity evaluation methods, including chemical, cellular, and animal assays, and discusses the main AI workflow, covering dataset construction, molecular representation, machine-learning and deep-learning models, structure-aware and multimodal approaches, and model interpretability. Potential applications in peptide generation, risk stratification, process optimization, validation design, and quality control are also highlighted.
Key findings and conclusions
Peptide toxicity prediction has evolved from handcrafted descriptors, such as amino acid composition, dipeptide frequency, motifs, and physicochemical properties, to protein language models, predicted three-dimensional structures, geometric graphs, and atomic-level chemical representations. Deep-learning and multimodal models improve the integration of sequence, structural, and chemical information. However, inconsistent toxicity endpoints, unreliable negative samples, homologous sequence leakage, limited external validation, and insufficient consideration of food processing and dietary exposure remain major challenges. Future studies should develop food-oriented datasets, calibrated and interpretable models, and closed-loop validation frameworks linking computational prediction with digestion, cell, animal, and quality-control studies. AI-based toxicity prediction may support the safe development of food-derived peptides.

title: Artificial intelligence in alternative proteins: Integrating the structure–process–property framework across the value chain

ai4s_review.rationale: 综述AI在替代蛋白发现筛选、加工监测和配方优化中的实际作用，以质构、营养与安全性为食品科学终点。

verified_metadata.abstract:
Background
Alternative proteins are increasingly promoted as part of the response to sustainability, resource, and food security pressures. However, broader adoption remains limited by unstable functionality, sensory shortcomings, processing complexity, high cost, and poor transfer across materials and scales. These constraints arise because alternative proteins behave as coupled food systems in which composition, structure, process conditions, and product performance interact strongly.
Scope and approach
This review examines how artificial intelligence is being used across the alternative protein value chain, spanning upstream discovery and screening, midstream process monitoring and adaptive manufacturing, and downstream formulation, nutrition, safety, and consumer analysis. Rather than cataloging algorithms, the review evaluates AI through the practical decisions it supports across plant-based, fermentation-derived, insect, and cultivated protein systems.
Key findings and conclusions
Current evidence shows that AI is most credible when used for candidate prioritization, mechanism-aware annotation, soft sensing, constrained optimization, sensory mapping, and consumer insight generation, rather than for full automation. Progress remains uneven across protein categories and application stages, and many reported successes remain context-specific. The main barriers are fragmented data, weak standardization, limited transferability, inadequate uncertainty-aware validation, and poor integration with manufacturing and regulatory requirements. Future progress will depend on stronger data infrastructure, robustness-oriented benchmarking, human-validated workflows, and closer alignment between model outputs and food-relevant endpoints such as texture, flavor, nutrition, safety, and consumer acceptance, while keeping experimental validation central to translation into scalable, reliable, and evidence-based alternative protein systems for wider practical food industry deployment.

title: Artificial intelligence and digital twins: pathways to climate-resilient, traceable and equitable global food supply chains
ai4s_tags: AI for 地球宇宙科学

ai4s_review.rationale: 出版社标为Discussion；文章倡议AI数字孪生的食品供应链治理优先事项，属于观点讨论而非研究或实质方法综述。

verified_metadata.abstract:
Background
Climate shocks, supply chain interruptions, and persistent inequities continue to threaten the safety, quality, and sustainability of global food systems. Artificial intelligence (AI) and digital twins, high-fidelity virtual replicas continuously refreshed with real-time sensing, IoT, and blockchain data, offer powerful capabilities for optimization, prediction, and decision support
Scope and approach
This perspective argues that integrated AI-digital-twin frameworks can advance three interdependent priorities in food science and technology: (i) climate resilience through physics-informed modeling of refrigerated chains, dynamic shelf-life prediction, and adaptive preservation strategies; (ii) end-to-end traceability via tamper-evident, multi-stakeholder data flows that support real-time quality and safety monitoring; and (iii) social equity by lowering barriers for smallholder inclusion in formal processing and distribution networks while embedding equity constraints in optimization objectives. Drawing on recent implementations in processing, cold-chain logistics, and post-harvest systems, we synthesize demonstrated benefits in waste reduction, quality retention, and decision speed, while critically assessing technical, economic, and ethical barriers, including limited technology readiness levels (mostly TRL 4-6), data quality challenges in perishable matrices, machine bias, and the digital divide.
Key findings and conclusions
We argue that progress requires treating resilience, traceability, and equity as coequal optimization objectives rather than sequential add-ons. We propose priority actions focused on food-specific data standards for quality and safety parameters, validation infrastructure for hybrid physics-informed shelf-life and spoilage models, regulatory pathways for AI-supported food safety decisions, and longitudinal studies that measure processing yield, nutritional retention, and post-harvest waste outcomes throughout diverse contexts. Without deliberate attention to these engineering and governance gaps, AI-digital twins risk widening rather than narrowing existing divides in global food systems.

title: Tropical fruit-derived starches as emerging bioeconomic resources: Extraction, physicochemical properties, and applications (2020–2025): A systematic review
abstract: The growing demand for sustainable biomaterials and circular bioeconomy strategies has intensified the search for unconventional starch sources, particularly those recovered from fruits and agro-industrial by-products. These renewable resources represent promising alternatives to conventional starches while contributing to waste valorization and resource efficiency. This systematic review critically evaluates recent advances in starch extraction from unconventional fruit sources, emphasizing extraction technologies, structural and physicochemical characteristics, functional properties, modification strategies, and emerging industrial applications. The review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines and analyzed studies published between 2020 and 2025 retrieved from six scientific databases. Of the 475 records identified, 51 studies met the eligibility criteria and were included in the qualitative synthesis. The reviewed studies demonstrate that starches can be successfully recovered from different fruit tissues, including pulp, seeds, stems, and peels, using both green and conventional extraction methods, frequently achieving high extraction yields. Botanical origin, extraction methodology, and modification strategy were identified as the main factors governing starch morphology, crystallinity, thermal behavior, rheological performance, and technological functionality. While native starches are mainly applied as functional food ingredients and flour replacers, modified starches have increasingly expanded into high-value applications, including biodegradable packaging, smart films, encapsulation systems, pharmaceutical carriers, and other bio-based materials. The evidence also indicates a clear shift toward environmentally friendly extraction and modification technologies that support circular bioeconomy initiatives. Nevertheless, future research should prioritize standardized characterization protocols, pilot-scale validation, techno-economic assessment, life-cycle analysis, and artificial intelligence-assisted process optimization to accelerate the industrial implementation of unconventional fruit starches as sustainable biomaterials. • Systematic review of unconventional fruit-derived starches published between 2020 and 2025 following PRISMA guidelines. • Unconventional starches were successfully extracted from fruit pulp, seeds, stems, and roots using conventional and green methods. • Significant variations in physicochemical and functional properties influenced technological and industrial applications. • Applications included food products, biodegradable films, bioplastics, and encapsulation systems for bioactive compounds. • Fruit-derived starches support waste valorization, sustainable resource use, and circular bioeconomy strategies.

title: From bean to bar 5.0: Artificial intelligence, sensing technologies and robotics across the cocoa–chocolate value chain
abstract: Background Cocoa and chocolate production face persistent challenges related to climate variability, pests and diseases, postharvest losses, quality inconsistency, traceability requirements and sustainability concerns. Advances in artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), sensing technologies, robotics and automation offer opportunities to improve productivity, quality management and operational efficiency across the cocoa–chocolate value chain. Scope and approach This review proposes an integrated bean-to-bar 5.0 framework that synthesizes recent applications of AI, ML, sensing systems, robotics and automation in cocoa farming, postharvest processing, quality and safety evaluation, chocolate product innovation, manufacturing, packaging and logistics. Studies involving computer vision, deep learning, electronic noses, spectroscopy, Internet of Things (IoT) platforms and robotic handling systems are analyzed with respect to datasets, algorithms, technology readiness and deployment constraints to identify current capabilities and future research needs. Key findings and conclusions AI-enabled vision, spectroscopic and sensor-based approaches show strong potential for cocoa pod disease detection, bean grading, and rapid, non-destructive cacao quality assessment, while AI-assisted inspection, 3D printing, robotic handling and automated packaging can enhance sorting accuracy, process consistency and operational efficiency in chocolate manufacturing. Yet most technologies remain at laboratory, pilot or prototype stages, constrained by narrow datasets, controlled testing conditions, fragmented interoperability and limited techno-economic or socio-technical evaluation. Future progress will require representative multimodal datasets, rigorous field and factory validation, interoperable digital ecosystems, responsible AI governance and human-centred automation strategies tailored to smallholder-dominated cocoa regions. Overall, AI, sensing and robotics offer considerable potential to support more efficient, traceable, resilient and sustainable cocoa–chocolate systems.

title: Artificial intelligence-enabled strategies for addressing bottlenecks in probiotic development
abstract: Background Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied in microbiology; however, its integration into probiotic development remains limited. Existing reviews have primarily focused on isolated applications, leaving a gap in understanding the broader technical bottlenecks across the probiotic development pipeline and how AI can systematically address them. Scope and approach This review adopts a bottleneck-oriented, stage-specific framework to evaluate the role of AI in probiotic development. The pipeline is structured into four key stages: mechanistic screening, stability screening, strain characterization, and product and process optimization. For each stage, major technical challenges are identified, and corresponding AI-driven strategies are critically assessed, with particular emphasis on data characteristics and analytical constraints. Key findings and conclusions AI demonstrates strong potential to overcome recurring challenges across the probiotic development pipeline. These include limitations associated with small-sample, high-dimensional, and heterogeneous datasets in mechanistic screening; complex interactions among multiple stress factors and labor-intensive workflows in stability screening; strain-level heterogeneity and incomplete functional annotation in strain characterization; and large experimental design spaces, nonlinear variable interactions, and limited condition-specific data in product and process optimization. This review links these bottlenecks to actionable AI strategies and proposes a stepwise, sequencing data-centered workflow to facilitate systematic AI integration. Overall, the study provides a practical roadmap for advancing AI-enabled probiotic research and development.

title: Digital twins and physics-informed machine learning for safe agro-industrial waste valorization: Bioactive recovery, food-grade standardization, and regulatory readiness

verified_metadata.abstract:
Background
Agro-industrial residues are promising sources of phenolics, pigments, polysaccharides, proteins, and other functional ingredients, but food-grade valorization remains constrained by feedstock heterogeneity, sensor uncertainty, empirical scale-up, solvent and energy burdens, and contaminant co-extraction.
Scope and approach
This review critically evaluates digital twins and physics-informed machine learning (PIML) as a safety-bounded framework for residue valorization. It examines process analytical technology, laboratory assays, soft sensors, unit-operation models, model predictive control, techno-economic assessment, life-cycle assessment, and regulatory audit trails. Particular emphasis is placed on coupling target-bioactive recovery with the transport and concentration of pesticides, mycotoxins, metals, residual solvents, and process impurities.
Key findings and conclusions
PIML can embed transport, reaction, rheological, and degradation constraints into learning architectures, thereby improving extrapolation from sparse and drifting food-process datasets. Digital twins can extend these models into synchronized cyber-physical systems that optimize recovery while enforcing calibrated uncertainty, contaminant boundaries, explainability, traceability, and dossier-ready comparability for EFSA Novel Food, FDA GRAS, Codex, and related pathways. Persistent barriers include sensor fouling, calibration drift, missing benchmark datasets, computational latency, interoperability gaps, and limited toxicological validation. A staged maturity roadmap is proposed, from data shadows to qualified autonomous twins. An updated search through 6 June 2026 identified adjacent reviews, but no publicly indexed source jointly formalized PIML-constrained unit-operation twins, coupled bioactive-hazard states, uncertainty-bounded release invariants, and regulatory comparability. However, DT/PIML should be implemented as staged, risk-based decision-support systems, not universal replacements for conventional optimization, because scale-transfer uncertainty, rare-event coverage, and computational burden determine whether industrial use is justified.

title: Digitalization pathways for food loss and waste prevention in agri-food supply chains: Current evidence, challenges and future directions
abstract: Background Food loss and waste (FLW) remains a major challenge for global agri-food systems, generating substantial environmental, economic, and social impacts. Digitalization has emerged as a promising strategy to improve resource efficiency and support FLW prevention, yet the effectiveness of different digital technologies remains uneven and often insufficiently evaluated. Scope and approach This critical review examines the contribution of Industry 4.0 and Agriculture 4.0 technologies, including the Internet of Things (IoT), artificial intelligence (AI), big data analytics, blockchain, and consumer-oriented digital platforms, to FLW prevention across the entire agri-food supply chain. Rather than cataloguing technological applications, the review critically distinguishes between demonstrated reductions in FLW and improvements in technical performance that are frequently assumed to translate into waste prevention, while evaluating technological maturity, implementation barriers, and future research priorities. Key findings and conclusions IoT-enabled monitoring and smart logistics provide the strongest direct evidence for reducing spoilage risks; among AI applications, inventory management is comparatively well supported, although much of the broader AI/ML evidence remains based on operational proxies. Evidence for blockchain applications, dynamic pricing, and consumer-facing technologies remains limited or highly context dependent. Persistent barriers include fragmented data infrastructures, interoperability constraints, unequal digital capabilities, uncertain economic returns, and rebound effects. Digital technologies can contribute meaningfully to FLW prevention only when integrated with organizational, behavioural, and governance strategies. Future research should prioritize standardized impact metrics, longitudinal system-level evaluations, and integrated environmental assessments capable of quantifying real reductions in FLW and associated sustainability trade-offs.

title: Trustworthy and physics-informed artificial intelligence for food processing operations: validation, control relevance, and industrial readiness
abstract: ABSTRACT Background Artificial intelligence (AI) applications in food processing are mostly limited to data-driven prediction models, while industry needs AI for trustworthy operational use. Much of the evidence still rests on dataset-level performance, whereas validation quality, physical credibility, uncertainty, interpretability, control relevance, and industrial readiness of AI models are examined less consistently. Scope and approach This critical review uses structured evidence mapping strategy to appraise recent reviews, methodological papers, and direct evidence studies across drying, thermal processing, extrusion, fermentation, cleaning, quality monitoring and process systems enabled by AI models. Related nonthermal, membrane, separation, and rheology-oriented studies are used only when they inform validation, process physics, monitoring, control, or industrial readiness. The final reference list contains 73 cited sources; 69 of these were coded as records in the structured evidence map, while the remaining sources supported background, conceptual framing, methodological context, or boundary positioning. Key findings and conclusions Predictive modeling and soft sensing are comparatively mature, especially when spectral, imaging, acoustic, or process data are used to estimate quality attributes or state variables. However, external validation across batches, products, equipment, and production periods remains inconsistent. Uncertainty is rarely quantified, and many claims involving digital twins or advanced control remain limited to conceptual frameworks, simulations, or laboratory-scale demonstrations. Physics-informed machine learning, hybrid mechanistic data-driven models, reduced-order models and digital twins offer promising pathways toward transferable and robust process AI, but only when underlying physical assumptions, validation domains, and deployment constraints are clearly defined. Future research should better align model claims with rigorous validation strategies, explicit physical grounding, uncertainty quantification, and measurable process-level benefits.

title: Sustainable transformation of rare earth metals value chain for dual-use technologies
abstract: Rare earth metals (REMs), including lanthanides, scandium, and yttrium, are crucial for civilian and defense applications owing to their superior magnetic, optical, and catalytic properties. Their strategic importance extends to clean energy, electric vehicles, corrosion protection, agriculture, catalysis, and advanced weaponry. Although abundant in Earth’s crust, rare earth elements (REEs) are geologically dispersed and economically challenging to extract owing to similar ionic properties, creating supply chain risk largely attributed to China’s refinery capacity. In this review, we analyze the entire REM value chain, including classification, global distribution, mining, mineral processing, beneficiation (physical and chemical), leaching, and separation and purification, along with their high-performance applications. The geopolitical impact, market pressures, and processing complexities, including environmental hazards, purity management, and scale-up, are also discussed within the context of international policy responses. In response, strategies such as green metallurgy, closed-loop recycling, and green extraction techniques have been proposed to reduce environmental impact and supply vulnerability. A dual-use perspective is adopted, linking REEs 4f-driven properties to essential roles in both advanced civilian industries and defense technologies. Future pathways such as AI-enabled separation, digital tracking, and circular economy models are identified as routes to resilient and sustainable supply chains. By fostering innovation, diversification, and recycling, nations can reduce reliance on limited suppliers while meeting rising demand, thereby supporting sustainable growth and national security.

title: Lithiation-dependent solid electrolyte interphase nucleation pathways in Si/Li6PS5Cl interfaces uncovered by machine learning-accelerated simulations

ai4s_review.rationale: 机器学习力场模拟硅负极与固态电解质反应界面，揭示锂化状态相关的SEI成核和离子输运机制。

verified_metadata.abstract: Solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) formation mechanisms in silicon-anode all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs) remain the critical unresolved bottleneck for commercialization, hindered by experimental inaccessibility and fundamental limitations in simulating complex reactive interfaces across electrochemical conditions. We bridge this gap using a machine learning force field (MLFF) with sub-100 meV Å-1 accuracy, enabling large-scale, quantum-fidelity simulation of the full reactive interface. This comprehensive model (3072 atoms, 5 elements, 2000 ps) simultaneously captures the coupled dynamics of silicon lithiation, electrolyte decomposition, and SEI formation. The results reveal that SEI nucleation initiates predominantly at the highly lithiated stage, driven by chemo-mechanical strain-induced dissociation of thiophosphate units (<50 ps). The self-assembled SEI evolves into a compositionally graded bilayer: a Li+-deficient Li2S/LiCl-rich electrolyte-adjacent matrix and a Li+-abundant Li2S/Li3P-dominated anode-proximal zone, delivering exceptional ionic conductivity (27.2 mS cm-1) via Li2S percolation highways. However, this structure exhibits mechanical vulnerability (8.11 GPa modulus) and defect-mediated electronic leakage. Finally, we establish lithiation-state control and interface engineering as dual design principles to overcome SEI-driven failure. This work provides an atomic-resolution framework for rationally designing degradation-resistant ASSBs, fundamentally accelerating the transition from empirical optimization to knowledge-driven battery engineering.

title: Representation learning accelerates the development of models for Li-ion battery health diagnostics and prognostics

ai4s_review.rationale: 综述表征学习在锂电池健康诊断与预测中的应用，明确生成式增广和迁移学习应对新化学体系及工况。

verified_metadata.abstract: In recent years, the evolution of Li-ion battery material components, cell architectures, and application scenarios has posed significant challenges for the rapid adaptation of battery management systems (BMS). Accurate health diagnostics and prognostics are fundamental to reliable battery operation. However, traditional approaches based on empirical equations, physical models, or handcrafted features often suffer from limited generalization, heavy data demands, and time-consuming development. Representation learning, a major advancement in deep learning, is emerging as a powerful tool to accelerate battery health modeling. Under novel chemistries and unseen operating conditions, it mitigates data scarcity through generative learning and enables rapid model adaptation via transfer learning, which was overlooked in earlier reviews. We systematically summarize representation learning architectures tailored for battery data, highlight their applications in data augmentation and cross-domain transfer, and further identify key challenges and future opportunities in data privacy, multimodal information integration, and model interpretability. Overall, representation learning establishes a solid foundation for the efficient development of next-generation intelligent BMS.

title: Suppressing dendrites in lithium metal anodes: A review of passivation layers and multiscale computational approaches
abstract: Lithium metal batteries (LMBs) have shown significant interest as next-generation energy storage systems due to their ultra-high theoretical specific capacity of 3,860 mAh g −1 . However, dendrite growth remains a major obstacle to commercialization, driven by instabilities in the native passivation layer (NPL) and the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). The NPL, formed by lithium’s reactivity with ambient gases, induces uneven current distributions, while fragile SEIs crack easily, exposing fresh lithium and triggering parasitic reactions. This review combines experimental and computational approaches to understand and improve these interfacial layers. For the NPL, mechanothermal milling, picosecond laser treatments, vacuum thermal evaporation, and engineered electrodeposition layers have been employed to smooth surfaces and lower resistance. For the SEI, approaches such as artificial SEIs, electrolyte additives, solid-state electrolytes (SSEs), anode modification, and separator engineering enhance stability and suppress dendrite growth. Complementarily, computational methods including density functional theory (DFT), molecular dynamics (MD), ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD), kinetic Monte Carlo (KMC), and machine learning (ML) provide atomistic insights into interfacial reactions and ion transport. Together, these experimental and computational approaches provide a unified framework that guides the design of stable interfacial layers and accelerates the safe commercialization of high-energy LMBs.

title: Regenerate large-scale retired second-life battery datasets via recovered capacity labels-based deep learning

ai4s_review.rationale: 深度学习融合电池领域知识恢复退役电池容量标签，在96块真实电池上验证，支持健康退化数据集构建。

verified_metadata.abstract: Accurate diagnosis of the health degradation of retired batteries is crucial for ensuring their safe and reliable reuse. While machine learning offers promising solutions, training models to overcome the high heterogeneity of retired batteries requires massive degradation data, leading to high testing costs and substantial energy waste. Here, we reveal the potential to recover large-scale and high-quality second-life battery datasets from field data to assist in diagnosing the health of retired batteries. By seamlessly fusing deep learning and domain knowledge, we enabled the accurate recovery of capacity labels for operating data without regular fully charging or discharging calibrations. To validate the proposed method, we develop a large-scale degradation test on 96 realistic retired batteries, performing over 50,000 charge/discharge cycles to simulate different stationary energy storage scenarios with 24 charge-discharge intervals. With only 3 capacity measurements available over the second-life, the proposed method accurately recovers the capacity labels with a root mean square error below 30 mAh. Furthermore, the health diagnostic model trained on regenerated dataset is comparable to the model trained on real data, with an almost negligible error of less than 5 mAh. More importantly, we expect to save at least 98% of test time, electricity and energy consumption to generate datasets cost-effectively. This study highlights the potential of field data to bridge the critical data gap in diagnosing the health degradation of retired batteries.

title: Interpretable enhanced-ECFP-guided deep learning for rational electrolyte design and Coulombic efficiency prediction in lithium metal batteries

ai4s_review.rationale: 分子指纹神经网络预测电解液库仑效率，并据解释结果设计经电化学实验验证的电解液。

verified_metadata.abstract: Rational electrolyte design is essential for enhancing the Coulombic efficiency (CE) and interfacial stability of lithium metal batteries. However, current molecular representations limited in their description of molecular connectivity and lacking substructure frequency information constrain the development of accurate and interpretable AI models. This paper introduces an interpretable AI framework to predict CE using an enhanced extended-connectivity fingerprint representation that integrates molecular type, substructure frequency, and concentration weighting. A dataset of 168 CE values from Li–Cu half–cells was used to train a deep neural network, which outperformed conventional methods in predictive accuracy. SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis identified fluorine-containing and cyclic ether motifs as key structural features for high CE. Accordingly, a fluorine-rich, cyclic-ether-based electrolyte (1 M lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide in methyltetrahydrofuran and 1,1,2,2-tetrafluoroethyl 2,2,3,3-tetrafluoropropyl ether (1:3 v/v)) achieved a CE of 99.72% in Li–Cu cells and excellent cycling stability in lithium–lithium iron phosphate full cells. This framework can facilitate AI-based molecular design for electrochemical energy storage and conversion.

title: HA-LLM: A domain knowledge-enhanced large language model for vehicle-cloud collaborative battery health awareness

ai4s_review.rationale: 领域适配大语言模型估计动力电池健康状态，结合充电时序和不确定性校正，在实车及拆解容量测试验证。

verified_metadata.abstract: Accurate state of health (SOH) estimation for electric vehicle traction batteries is critical for safety and reliability, yet real-world operation exhibits nonlinear aging and pronounced distribution shifts across vehicles. Large language models (LLMs) offer transferable priors that can improve sample efficiency. However, they are pretrained on discrete text, creating a representation gap for continuous, physically constrained battery signals, and their generative inference may yield physically inconsistent numerical outputs. This work proposes a battery domain knowledge-enhanced health awareness LLM framework (HA-LLM). HA-LLM aligns resampled charging current sequences with the LLM embedding space via heterogeneous modal semantic alignment, enabling physically consistent representations. It also injects battery degradation priors via information-bottleneck-inspired prefix adaptation, enabling domain adaptation while retaining the pretrained backbone’s general reasoning ability. To mitigate hallucination risk, an uncertainty-aware module estimates predictive uncertainty via Monte Carlo sampling and triggers selective substitution with a physics-consistent estimator. The framework is validated using one-year field vehicle data from 100 production vehicles on a vehicle-cloud platform and an independent battery teardown and bench capacity calibration on an unseen vehicle model. HA-LLM consistently outperforms strong baselines and remains robust in few-shot and zero-shot evaluations that stress cross-vehicle generalization.

title: Physics-informed machine learning exploration of Na storage mechanisms in disordered carbon

ai4s_review.rationale: 机器学习原子势与无监督结构分析揭示硬碳中的钠扩散模式及结构输运关系。

verified_metadata.abstract: Sodium-ion batteries are a cost-effective, sustainable alternative to lithium-ion systems for large-scale energy storage. However, optimizing sodium storage in carbon-based anodes with microstructural complexity and atomic disorder remains a major challenge. The intrinsic inhomogeneity of these materials produces diverse local environments, making it difficult for conventional methods to predict and control ion dynamics. Hard carbon (HC) anodes, composed of ranges of ordered-to-disordered graphitic and amorphous nanodomains, offer tunable ion storage and rate capacity, yet rationale design remains a challenge due to poorly understood correlation between local atomic feature and ion transport mechanism. To address this challenge, we introduce a data-driven framework that integrates validated machine-learned interatomic potentials, large-scale molecular dynamics simulations, and machine learning to elucidate sodium transport mechanisms as a function of carbon and sodium loading densities. By computing per-ion structural descriptors and applying unsupervised learning, we identify distinct diffusion modes governed by microscopic features. Supervised analysis and correlation mapping then establish quantitative links between these transport regimes and processing variables such as bulk carbon density and sodium content. This physics-informed approach establishes quantitative structure–transport relationships and offers actionable design principles for engineering high-performance HC anodes.

title: Data-driven surrogate modelling and calibration of particle breakage in Li-ion electrode calendering
abstract: This study introduces a comprehensive, data-driven framework for efficient simulation and calibration of particle breakage during lithium-ion battery electrode calendering. We first proposed a Discrete Element Methode (DEM) based spherical damage model realised via a particular particle replacement mechanism, and generated a broad training set by uniformly varying eight model parameters. On this basis, a novel dual-branch neural network is trained to reproduce both the full compaction-pressure profile and the statistical distribution of fracture events, achieving high fidelity against held-out simulations. This surrogate model is embedded within a two-stage inverse-optimisation routine that infers breakage parameters directly from experimental pressure-depth data, yielding calibrated inputs for rapid forward prediction. With the help of surrogate efficiency, a global Sobol analysis quantifies the relative importance of each parameter, guiding model simplification work and highlighting the roles of characteristic size and fracturing fitting exponent. The coupled DEM-Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) studies reveal that allowing particle breakage during heavy calendering appreciably lowers tortuosity and enhances effective diffusivity compared to non-fracturing scenarios, with larger initial particle sizes further improving transport pathways. Collectively, this work delivers a scalable and advanced approach for parameter estimation, sensitivity assessment, and design optimisation of electrode microstructures under realistic processing conditions.

title: Hybrid experts-decoupled and physics-informed neural network for lithium-ion battery degradation modeling and prognosis

ai4s_review.rationale: 物理信息专家网络解耦电池退化过程并估计健康状态，验证跨电极和工况迁移能力。

verified_metadata.abstract: Accurate estimation of the State of Health (SOH) for lithium-ion batteries is crucial for extending service life and mitigating safety risks. However, the prevailing data-driven approaches for SOH estimation regard the internal degradation mechanisms as a black box, resulting in significant challenges such as high data requirements for complex physical models, limited model transferability, and poor electrochemical interpretability. To address these challenges with precision and comprehensiveness, we propose a hybrid experts-decoupled and physics-informed neural network (HyED-PINN), which decouples the degradation behavior and different physical fields. The HyED-PINN leverages expert models for different physical fields to extract electrochemical quantities, and employs physics-informed loss functions to train and recouple the related quantities for accurate SOH estimation. Notably, the sufficient transferability of HyED-PINN is validated by the combination of diverse datasets (electrode types, charge/discharge protocols, and operating conditions). The proposed model achieves high prediction accuracy, with the lowest RMSE reaching 0.54% on the CALCE dataset and remaining below 1.6% across all evaluated datasets. Compared with conventional neural networks, the HyED-PINN exhibits superior performance in small-sample scenarios, enhanced transfer learning capability, and importantly improved electrochemical interpretability. Overall, this study highlights the promise of physics-informed machine learning for accurate SOH estimation and extends its applicability to real-time risk detection of physical fields during battery operation.

title: BMINN: Learning chemical potentials and parameters from voltage data for multi-phase battery modeling
abstract: Free-energy landscapes and chemical potentials govern the dynamics of phase transitions, transport, and stability in functional materials, yet they remain experimentally inaccessible under realistic operating conditions. Here we introduce a Bayesian model-integrated neural network (BMINN) that embeds physics-based formulations of non-autonomous partial differential–algebraic equations into probabilistic learning. This approach reconstructs hidden thermodynamics directly from macroscopic current–voltage data, providing quantitative access to metastable states, staging transitions, and energy barriers without synchrotron probes. Demonstrated on lithium–graphite electrodes, BMINN recovers full Gibbs free-energy landscapes with fidelity validated against operando X-ray diffraction. The framework generalizes across dynamical regimes, enabling accurate voltage prediction, internal state estimation, and inference of governing parameters. Beyond batteries, BMINN exemplifies a broadly applicable strategy for learning missing physics in multiphase, non-equilibrium systems, offering a new pathway to uncover hidden thermodynamic functions across condensed matter and materials physics.

title: Fast and direct diagnosis of states of health of spent batteries
abstract: Abstract Fast diagnosis of state of health (SoH) is essential for a second life of the spent batteries due to drastically increasing demands for lithium-ion batteries. However, additional voltage or state of charge (SoC) settings were needed to predict SoH. Here, we suggest a SoH prediction process without any additional settings within 110 seconds (maximum 290 seconds) using machine learning, which consists of 2 steps: protocol classification and SoH regression. Data were generated from 18650-sized cells. There are 3 protocols depending on SoC due to cut-off voltage, and open-circuit voltage and 1.0 C-rate discharge voltage for 10 seconds were collected at every 5% SoC in 188 SoH. The protocol classification model showed 0.9985 of accuracy. Then, protocol data, with current pulses and rest times, corresponding to SoC were collected at every 5% SoC in 1043 SoH, and 12 features were selected from 60 features. The SoH regression model showed 0.850% mean absolute error (MAE), and performance in cases of untrained SoC and misclassification was also superior because the model was trained on all SoC data. In addition, the suggested SoH prediction process can apply to untrained cells, such as different form factors. The performances of 21700-sized cells were improved to 2.600% MAE through feature engineering to the resistance-related features using the ratio between cell capacity and external volume. This paper highlights a fast and direct SoH prediction process without any settings, and feature engineering of untrained cell data to save time and energy for diagnosis of spent batteries.

title: Visualizing lithium-rich manganese-based layered oxides: Advancing dynamic monitoring to decipher battery chemistry
abstract: Lithium-rich manganese oxides (LRMOs) show great promise as high capacity, cost effective cathodes for next-generation Li-ion batteries, Nevertheless, they still confront issues such as voltage decline, capacity loss, and structural instability. Recent breakthroughs in in situ / operando characterization methods have emerged as highly effective means for uncovering the dynamic changes in structure and electrochemical activity of these materials. This review delves into advanced methodologies enabling the real time observation of phase alterations, oxygen redox interactions, and the migration of transition metals (TMs) throughout the battery's charge/discharge cycles. By combining various characterization tools, researchers can reveal crucial connections between defect formation, redox mechanisms, and the stability of the battery's structure, enabling the development of novel approaches to suppress performance degradation. The study illustrates that mechanistic insights into phase transitions and failure modes, gained through advanced characterization, are instrumental in improving LRMOs. Prioritizing multiscale in situ methodologies coupled with machine learning for data interpretation will be crucial for rapidly developing viable LRMOs. These advancements in real time analysis hold promise for addressing current limitations and fast tracking the market introduction of high-energy-density materials for future energy storage.

title: Unveiling electrochemical heterogeneity: A physics-informed graph clustering framework for retired batteries

ai4s_review.rationale: 对比图学习结合弛豫时间谱聚类电池电化学特性，用于退役电芯分组并验证组装电池一致性。

verified_metadata.abstract: The large-scale retirement of lithium-ion batteries necessitates reliable strategies for second-life utilization, particularly in the face of pronounced cell-to-cell variation. We propose a two-stage framework that converts heterogeneity derived from distribution of relaxation times (DRT) analysis into application-oriented module configurations. In the first stage, an unsupervised clustering approach integrates DRT analysis with contrastive graph learning. Normalized DRT spectra are used to construct a similarity graph based on Jensen–Shannon divergence. This process identifies cells that share similar kinetic characteristics. In the second stage, a greedy sliding window strategy is employed to match residual capacities. By ensuring that grouped cells exhibit both similar capacities and consistent electrochemical characteristics, this strategy reduces incompatibilities that cannot be captured by scalar capacity metrics alone. The framework was validated using 187 commercial NCA cylindrical cells, achieving a modularity of 0.6711 and a residual capacity prediction error of 0.88% (MAPE). The consistency of the assembled battery packs was verified through dynamic cycling behavior and relaxation process analyses. Further evaluation on 35 NCM pouch cells at both 0% and 20% SOC demonstrates stable clustering results across chemistries and SOC, confirming the robustness of the framework and its feasibility for integration into industrial recycling workflows. This study provides a scalable pathway for intelligent sorting and reliable second-life deployment of retired batteries.

title: Calorimetry-free identification of battery reaction kinetics using simulation-driven deep learning

ai4s_review.rationale: 模拟训练神经网络并迁移到实验数据，从温度响应反演电池反应动力学及边界参数。

verified_metadata.abstract: Reaction kinetic parameters quantitatively characterize the electrochemical and thermal behaviours of batteries, serving as critical inputs for thermal runaway (TR) modelling. However, their identification relies on calorimetric data, such as Accelerating Rate Calorimetry and Differential Scanning Calorimetry, which are costly, time-consuming, expertise-dependent, and limited in transferability across different battery chemistries and states. In this work, we present a generalizable framework for directly extracting reaction kinetic parameters from abuse tests, eliminating the need for calorimetric data. The framework combines simulation-driven deep learning with transfer learning. Initially, datasets are generated through dimensionality-reduced sampling and high-throughput TR simulations. A multi-stage neural network is trained on these datasets to map battery temperature evolution to the corresponding kinetic and boundary parameters. Transfer learning adapts the pre-trained model to the limited experimental datasets, addressing the cross-domain inconsistencies. The proposed method achieves accurate identification in both reaction kinetics and boundary conditions, with mean absolute percentage error less than 6.2% for key indicators in simulated battery temperature curves. The framework demonstrates strong generalizability across major commercial cell formats and chemistries. This study streamlines the workflow of kinetic parameter identification and reduces testing and analysis time, thus accelerating battery safety characterization and TR modelling.

title: Unlocking anode-free battery performance: AI-enhanced electron microscopy for deciphering layered cathode interfaces

ai4s_review.rationale: 综述AI增强电镜去噪与缺陷识别，用于分析无负极电池层状正极界面和结构性能关系。

verified_metadata.abstract: The pursuit of high-energy-density anode-free batteries (AFBs) has shifted the research focus toward the fundamental understanding of structural stability and interfacial chemistry. Layered cathode materials are central to this transition, yet their practical application in AFBs is hindered by complex failure mechanisms such as lattice strain and parasitic side reactions. This review systematically traces the evolution of advanced transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and its pivotal role in elucidating the structure-property relationships of these electrode materials. By integrating artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) for high-throughput data processing, we highlight how modern characterization overcomes traditional limitations in image denoising and automated defect recognition. The discussion encompasses both lithium and sodium-ion systems, focusing on in situ and cryogenic TEM techniques that reveal real-time ion migration, phase transformations, and the evolution of fragile solid-electrolyte interphases. Furthermore, we emphasize the interdisciplinary synergy between electron microscopy and AI as a necessity for the “mechanism-driven” design of next-generation and high-stability batteries. This review provides critical insights into addressing the bottlenecks of layered cathode configurations. Furthermore, this review discusses the emerging role of AI in integrating fragmented research data into structured knowledge graphs. By organizing highly heterogeneous experimental findings into relational networks, AI can uncover latent structure-performance correlations, offering a data-driven roadmap for mechanism-guided material design and advanced characterization.

title: The rise of an intelligent partner: How machine learning is reshaping electrolyte research and development

ai4s_review.rationale: 综述机器学习电解液筛选、性能预测、生成式分子设计与实验闭环优化。

verified_metadata.abstract: The development of high-performance electrolytes for advanced lithium batteries is pivotal for the energy transition but remains hindered by the inefficiencies of traditional trial-and-error approaches. The intricate balance among energy density, safety, and cycle life constitutes a complex multi-objective optimization problem that challenges conventional methods. Recently, machine learning (ML) has emerged as a transformative tool, shifting the electrolyte research paradigm from experience-driven to data-model-driven design. This review systematically outlines the progression of ML in electrolyte research, commencing with its role in high-throughput screening and performance prediction. We highlight the recent advent of generative models for de novo molecular design and the establishment of closed-loop "dry-wet" experimental systems, which achieve weekly iterative optimization. These advancements are poised to accelerate the discovery of electrolytes tailored for next-generation batteries. Finally, we critically discuss the persisting challenges, such as data standardization, multi-scale modeling, and human-machine collaboration, and propose feasible solutions to pave the way for an intelligent and autonomous future in electrolyte innovation.

title: NASICON-type LATP solid electrolytes for lithium metal batteries: Fundamentals to AI-driven materials design

ai4s_review.rationale: Energy Storage Materials正式综述设有专节Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) for advanced LATP solid electrolytes，讨论掺杂筛选、烧结优化与结构稳定性，直接服务固态电解质材料设计。

verified_metadata.abstract: NASICON-type Li1+xAlxTi2-x(PO4)3 (LATP) is a promising solid electrolyte for lithium metal batteries because of its high ionic conductivity, stability in air, and relatively low processing cost. However, its practical use is limited by the reduction of Ti4+ at the lithium interface, which leads to the formation of a mixed-conducting interphase and promotes dendrite growth. In addition, high grain-boundary resistance significantly reduces the overall ionic conductivity. This review outlines key strategies to address these challenges, including doping to improve ionic conductivity and stability, interfacial engineering (protective interlayers, alloy buffers, and artificial SEI layers), and polymer–LATP composites to enhance interfacial contact and mechanical properties. Based on recent research, LATP performs more reliably in hybrid or composite systems than as a standalone electrolyte, where interfacial instability is difficult to control. Furthermore, this study highlights the emerging role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) in accelerating dopant selection, optimizing sintering processes, and enhancing structural stability. The practical realization of LATP-based solid-state batteries will depend on the synergistic integration of interfacial engineering, composite electrolyte design, and AI-driven materials optimization, where AI enables faster, cost-effective development of advanced materials.

title: Tri-modal machine learning powers efficient catalyst discovery for high-performance energy storage

ai4s_review.rationale: 图、文本和元素三模态模型筛选钾硫电池催化剂，候选材料经实验与机理表征验证。

verified_metadata.abstract: Overcoming the polysulfide shuttle effect is the critical challenge for developing high-performance potassium-sulfur (K-S) batteries. While designing catalyst materials is a promising route, the vast compositional space makes traditional screening impractical. Machine learning (ML) offers an approach to accelerate this process but suffers from the challenge of creating comprehensive feature representations and a lack of interpretability. To address these two challenges, we propose a tri-modal machine learning framework that interactively integrates graph, text, and elemental information. This framework employs a sophisticated fusion strategy based on multi-head cross-attention, which creates a rich, context-aware, and synergistic embedding that serves as a powerful feature representation. Moreover, it uses a component-level approach to interpretability by validating the quality of the textual features through attention score analysis. Using this framework, a high-throughput screening of over 75,000 configurations identified Ni-doped and Zn/Ti-co-doped CuS as promising candidates. Their superior electrochemical performance was confirmed by experiments. Further mechanistic insights from in situ and ex situ characterizations corroborate accelerated sulfur conversion kinetics. Additionally, the framework’s versatility was validated on diverse external datasets, spanning chemically and structurally distinct material systems and their associated bulk and surface properties. This work establishes a validated tri-modal ML framework that can provide a rapid, reliable, and interpretable pathway to accelerate the discovery of diverse, high-performance energy materials.

title: AI-enabled cross-scale modeling and parameter transfer for lithium-ion batteries

ai4s_review.rationale: 综述AI在电池跨尺度模型参数反演、代理模拟与物理量传递中的作用，面向电池状态及安全性建模。

verified_metadata.abstract: Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) are central to electric transportation and renewable-energy storage, yet their performance, aging, and safety are governed by coupled processes spanning atomic reactions, electrode microstructures, cell behavior, and module-level operation. Although mechanistic modeling and artificial intelligence (AI) have advanced rapidly, most studies remain confined to a single scale, task, or algorithm; consequently, the systematic transfer, compression, updating, and deployment of cross-scale physical quantities remain insufficiently understood. Here we present the AI-enabled Cross-scale Parameter Chain (ACPC), a carrier-centered framework for organizing cross-scale modeling and parameter transfer in LIBs under practical operating conditions. ACPC tracks how intrinsic quantities generated by density functional theory, molecular dynamics, machine-learning interatomic potentials, porous-electrode theory and pseudo-two-dimensional models, phase-field and electrochemical–mechanical models, equivalent-circuit models, and high-fidelity multiphysics simulations are transformed, compressed, validated, and updated across atom/molecule-to-electrode, electrode-to-cell, and cell-to-module/system interfaces. By evaluating AI according to interface-specific functions—including prior generation, parameter inversion, microstructure reconstruction, surrogate acceleration, uncertainty handling, online recalibration, diagnosis, and control optimization—rather than algorithmic categories alone, ACPC identifies where AI preserves or compromises physical traceability. The analysis shows that deployable battery intelligence requires transferable, identifiable, and updatable parameter carriers, rather than preservation of all lower-scale details, to support state estimation, health prognosis, fast-charging control, safety management, and digital-twin operation. This framework provides a roadmap for integrating multiscale physics, data-driven learning, and battery management to enable reliable and interpretable next-generation battery systems.

verified_metadata.abstract: Lithium metal batteries (LMBs) are widely regarded as promising next-generation energy storage solutions because of their high theoretical energy density. Nonetheless, their practical application is hindered by complex interfacial phenomena, including unstable solid electrolyte interphases (SEI), dendritic lithium growth, and ongoing electrolyte consumption, which cause rapid performance decline and safety concerns. Traditional experimental and computational methods often struggle to capture the multiscale and dynamic nature of these processes. Recent progress in machine learning (ML) offers new opportunities to speed up LMB development through data-driven materials discovery, mechanistic insights, and performance prediction. This review summarizes recent advances in applying ML to LMBs from three key perspectives: materials design, interfacial processes, and lifetime prediction. It highlights how ML models facilitate electrolyte discovery, elucidate the mechanisms of SEI formation and dendrite growth, and predict battery degradation through early-cycle signals and morphological features. Finally, this review explores emerging opportunities for combining ML with high-throughput experimentation and autonomous laboratories to facilitate the closed-loop discovery of advanced battery technologies, as well as discusses the key challenges and future directions of ML-driven LMB research. This review is expected to provide not only a critical assessment of the state of the art but also a practical roadmap for integrating predictive analytics into next-generation battery research.

title: Interlayer-enhanced thermal management in lithium-ion batteries: A review on state-of-the-art modeling approaches
abstract: High-performance batteries, particularly Li-ion batteries, have emerged as the key elements of today’s energy systems. In such batteries, rapid charging and discharging can generate localized heat within the cells and trigger thermal runaway, which is extremely unsafe and harmful to the device. Therefore, optimal thermal management is critical for the safe and stable operation of Li-ion batteries under high-power conditions. One of the effective measures for this has proven to be introducing cooling interlayers between adjacent cells, promoting uniform temperature distribution and enhanced stability of the battery. Rigorous modeling and simulation of the thermal performance of batteries equipped with interlayer cooling mechanisms are very complex but critically important. Such models enable the investigation of proposed designs under various scenarios and specifications, while extending results solely through experimental studies is costly and demanding. This article presents a systematic review and assessment of a wide range of analytical and numerical modeling methods used in thermal management and optimization of Li-ion batteries. For this, the main mechanisms of heat production within cells, including Joule heating, heat from electrochemical reactions, entropy changes, and heat transfer processes, are first described. Then, the efficiency of a variety of interlayers in mitigating local hotspots and achieving a uniform temperature distribution are analyzed. The most common challenges of analytical, numerical, and multiscale approaches are evaluated, and the research gaps are highlighted. Finally, future prospects, including optimal layer design, predictive AI-based or data-driven models, and real-time simulations, are discussed. This review distinguishes itself by providing a dedicated modeling-oriented analysis of cell-to-cell interlayers, explicitly linking their material properties and structural roles to thermal behavior and performance at the battery module level.

title: Machine learning-assisted materials design, mechanistic insights, and predictive modeling for high performance lithium-sulfur batteries

verified_metadata.abstract: The development of high-energy-density lithium-sulfur batteries is crucial for sustainable progress, given their significant potential in long-duration energy storage, electric transportation, and low-carbon energy systems. Despite significant progress, practical Li-S battery operation is still limited by the lithium polysulfides shuttle effect, complex interfacial reactions, and poorly understood cross-scale degradation mechanisms. These challenges remain difficult to analyze using conventional experimental and theoretical approaches. Recently, machine learning, as a data-driven approach, has been widely adopted in lithium-sulfur battery research, demonstrating unique advantages in material design, reaction mechanism interpretation, and operational state prediction. This paper comprehensively reviews representative advancements in machine learning applications within this field. At the material level, data-driven models enable efficient screening and performance optimization of cathode catalysts, electrolyte systems, functional separators, and protective materials for lithium metal anodes. Regarding mechanisms, integrating machine learning with density functional theory expedites the prediction and analysis of lithium polysulfides adsorption behavior, reaction energy barriers, and key structural descriptors. Furthermore, in synergy with advanced physicochemical characterization techniques, this integration elucidates lithium polysulfides conversion and interfacial evolution. For operational aspects, machine learning algorithms are employed to predict critical parameters such as voltage response, capacity fade, and state of health under complex operating conditions. Finally, this review discusses current challenges and future directions for machine learning in lithium-sulfur battery research. Such an interdisciplinary machine learning approach will accelerate the advancement of lithium-sulfur batteries towards higher specific energy, longer lifespan, and engineering applications.

title: Rapid impedance spectrum extraction from relaxation signals via a battery kinetics-informed neural network

ai4s_review.rationale: 物理信息神经网络从短时弛豫信号重建阻抗谱并分解电化学动力学过程。

verified_metadata.abstract: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) enables the characterization of multiple battery kinetic processes and serves as a crucial tool for state estimation and mechanistic analysis. However, conventional EIS relies on frequency-sweep measurements, which are time-consuming and constrain its applicability to online monitoring and embedded systems. This work proposes a physics-informed neural network incorporating a mechanism-guided peak-fixed distribution of relaxation times (DRT) for impedance spectrum prediction. The mechanism-guided peak-fixed DRT-represents EIS using a small set of parameters, including amplitudes and relaxation time centers explicitly associated with dominant electrochemical kinetic processes. These parameters are embedded into an encoder-decoder architecture, enabling impedance spectrum reconstruction and kinetic process decoupling directly from relaxation signals with as few as 15 relaxation data points. A physics-informed loss function is further introduced to enforce physical consistency between the predicted impedance spectra and the DRT representations during training. Consequently, EIS estimation and electrochemical process decomposition are achieved in a mutually reinforcing manner. The proposed PINN delivers impedance prediction accuracy that is significantly superior to baseline models, while the extracted kinetic process parameters remain physically interpretable and can be directly used for activation energy validation and aging mechanism analysis. Overall, the proposed framework establishes a physically consistent approach for simultaneous EIS prediction and electrochemical kinetics analysis from time-domain relaxation signals.

title: A meta-learning framework for battery lifetime prediction across unseen operating conditions

ai4s_review.rationale: 元学习特征选择和跨分布训练预测未知工况的电池寿命，在多化学体系与温度协议数据上验证。

verified_metadata.abstract: Fast and reliable performance evaluation is essential for the development and deployment of next-generation battery technologies. However, comprehensive battery life testing across diverse operating conditions remains time-consuming and resource-intensive. Furthermore, efficient lifetime prediction is hindered by the absence of an effective modeling strategy that improves generalization across unseen operating conditions. Here, we introduce a systematic meta-learning framework for battery lifetime prediction that combines two key elements: a meta-designer for feature engineering, which identifies generalizable features by learning meta-level knowledge on how feature importance varies across operating conditions, and a meta-training strategy, which enhances generalization to unseen domains by simulating distribution shifts during training. Our framework is validated using three comprehensive datasets comprising 271 commercial lithium-ion cells with diverse operating conditions and electrode chemistries. Our approach achieves test errors of 8.9% and 6.7% for cycle life prediction under unseen distributions of cycling protocols and ambient temperatures, respectively. We further verify the robustness of the framework under diverse directions of distribution shift, and explore its extension to cross-chemistry transfer. Our meta-learning approach represents a breakthrough in the extrapolation capability of battery lifetime prediction under unseen operating conditions, and has the potential to significantly accelerate the development and deployment of next-generation batteries. This work highlights the promise of incorporating meta-learning into data-driven modeling to improve generalization ability in predicting the behavior of complex dynamical systems.

title: Machine learning surrogate modeling of materials extrusion for lithium-ion battery electrode dry manufacturing
abstract: Dry electrode manufacturing, such as extrusion and 3D-printing, offers a promising path toward more sustainable and cost-efficient lithium-ion battery production. However, optimizing extrusion-induced microstructure formation using only high-fidelity particle simulations remains computationally expensive. In this study, we develop a machine learning surrogate modeling framework to accelerate discrete element method (DEM)-based extrusion process analysis and inverse design. Six material and process parameters were selected using Latin Hypercube Sampling, and the corresponding evolutions of microstructure were generated from DEM simulations. The simulated time-dependent microstructure descriptors were further processed into quasi-steady state metrics, including void fraction, tortuosity factor, and effective (Binder and Carbon nanofiber)-network connectivity descriptors. Multiple regression algorithms were systematically benchmarked to construct fast surrogate models for predicting extrusion-induced microstructural states. The optimized models showed good predictive capability across the target descriptors, enabling rapid exploration of material-process-microstructure relationships at a substantially lower computational cost than direct DEM simulation. Shapley additive explanations were further employed to interpret parameter contributions and identify the dominant factors. The trained surrogate models were then coupled with single- and multi-objective optimization strategies to demonstrate inverse process design for targeted pore volume fraction, reduced tortuosity, and enhanced electronic connectivity. In addition, the time-series microstructural data were leveraged to further improve the predictive capability of the surrogate framework. This work establishes a data-efficient and interpretable workflow that integrates particle-scale simulations, machine learning, and process optimization, providing a scalable pathway for AI-accelerated manufacturing design of next-generation energy storage electrodes.

title: Artificial intelligence-assisted investigation of ion transport mechanisms and material screening for solid-state electrolytes

ai4s_review.rationale: 综述图网络、机器学习势及主动学习用于固态电解质筛选和离子输运机制分析。

verified_metadata.abstract: Solid-state electrolytes (SSEs) are central to the development of safe, high-energy-density all-solid-state batteries, yet their discovery remains constrained by the complex coupling of composition, crystal structure, defects, ion-transport pathways, interfaces and processing conditions. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers new opportunities to accelerate this process by integrating experimental data, materials databases, first-principles calculations and molecular-dynamics simulations. This review summarises recent progress in AI-assisted SSE research, with emphasis on data infrastructure, high-throughput screening, graph neural networks, machine-learning interatomic potentials, active learning, AI agents and closed-loop materials discovery. Particular attention is given to property prediction and mechanistic analysis, including ionic conductivity, migration barriers, diffusion pathways, interfacial stability, mechanical properties and multi-objective performance optimisation. The roles of AI in different electrolyte families, including oxides, sulfides, halides, polymers/composites, high-entropy systems and non-lithium conductors, are further discussed. Current challenges, such as limited and heterogeneous datasets, insufficient interpretability, weak cross-family transferability, inadequate representation of disorder and interfaces, and the gap between prediction and experimental validation, are critically examined. Finally, future directions are proposed based on standardised databases, physics-informed models, explainable AI, multi-objective active learning and autonomous AI–experiment workflows, aiming to advance SSE discovery from empirical screening toward mechanism-guided design.
