title: Leveraging machine learning for sustainable biochar and hydrochar production: Advances, challenges, and perspectives in thermochemical processes
authors: Sheikh Ahmad Faiz Sheikh Ahmad Tajuddin
abstract: The integration of machine learning (ML) into thermochemical processes—including pyrolysis, hydrothermal carbonization (HTC), gasification, and torrefaction—for biochar and hydrochar production from diverse organic wastes (e.g., food and agricultural residues, seafood, and shellfish processing by-products) has significantly advanced the understanding and optimization of these conversion technologies. Unlike previous reviews that focused on isolated processes or provided general overviews of ML applications, the present review offers a unique cross-process comparative framework that links modeling strategies, feature selection, and algorithm performance across all major thermochemical routes. Building on this comprehensive perspective, the review further examines the applications of biochar and hydrochar in renewable energy systems. It also explores the role of ML in accurately predicting key properties, including yield, composition, and calorific value. By optimizing process parameters and minimizing the need for extensive experimental trials, ML provides a data-driven approach to enhance process understanding and performance. Among thermochemical conversion methods, pyrolysis has been the most extensively investigated, and ensemble learning algorithms such as random forest regression and gradient boosting regression have demonstrated superior predictive accuracy. ML has also proven effective in modeling hydrochar characteristics in HTC, reinforcing its relevance to sustainable system development. However, the limited number of ML-based investigations on gasification and torrefaction constrains a more detailed comparative assessment, presenting opportunities for future research. This review highlights the importance of feature selection and dataset quality in ML modeling and emphasizes integrating ML into techno-economic and environmental assessments. Despite challenges in data availability and model generalization, advancements in sensor technologies and hybrid modeling approaches offer promise for real-time process monitoring. Overall, ML has strong potential to develop efficient, scalable, and sustainable biochar and hydrochar systems.

title: Applications of artificial intelligence for PVT heat pump systems: A review
abstract: In building heating and cooling field, photovoltaic-thermal (PVT) integrated with heat pump systems have become more and more attractive owing to their strengths of high energy efficiency and sustainability. However, the structure of PVT heat pump systems is complicated and it appears nonlinearity and dynamic characteristics in the operation process, thus posing significant challenges for control. Recently, artificial intelligence (AI) has garnered increasing attention as transformative tools for addressing these issues. On the basis of retrospecting and summarizing the novel PVT heat pump systems, the paper delves into a detailed analysis of AI applications in PVT heat pump systems, concentrating on four key areas: modeling, prediction, control and fault detection and diagnosis. The review outlines various AI approaches, including machine learning and deep reinforcement learning, and discusses their strengths and limitations when applied in PVT heat pump systems. Furthermore, the paper identifies key research deficiencies and promising pathways for the application of AI in this field.

title: Advances in artificial intelligence-enabled fault detection for virtual power plants
abstract: With the accelerating integration of renewable energy sources, virtual power plants (VPPs) have emerged as a key paradigm for aggregating and managing distributed energy resources. However, the inherent complexity, heterogeneity, and dynamic behavior of VPPs make them highly susceptible to faults, which can undermine system reliability, operational efficiency, and grid stability. Although previous research has examined specific aspects of fault diagnosis in VPPs, such as cyber threats and faults in individual resources, there is still a lack of comprehensive reviews that systematically address fault types and diagnostic methodologies across the entire VPP architecture. To address this gap, a structured and multi layered review of VPP fault diagnosis is presented. The VPP architecture is divided into three functional layers, namely aggregation, communication, and market interface, and the main fault types, cross layer interactions, and their potential impacts are analyzed in detail. In addition, a task oriented functional taxonomy of six representative artificial intelligence approaches, including feedforward neural networks, convolutional neural networks, recurrent neural networks, graph neural networks, federated learning, and reinforcement learning, is established. These methods are systematically reorganized and comparatively analyzed according to their roles, capabilities, and applicability across different VPP operational layers. Finally, the major challenges of deploying AI-driven methods in VPPs are identified, and future research directions are proposed to enhance the adaptability, scalability, and resilience of VPP systems, thereby supporting the reliable and sustainable operation of renewable energy-dominated grids.

title: Integrated assessment of energy systems: opportunities and barriers for digital twin and artificial intelligence adoption
abstract: Digital twins and artificial intelligence offer transformative capabilities for energy system assessment and present meaningful insights into the complex interplay between thermodynamic performance, economic viability, and environmental sustainability. In this Review, we examine the trends, major frameworks, assessment dimensions, and key barriers shaping integrated energy system evaluation. Roughly 12.7% of studies in the current literature integrate all four assessment dimensions-thermodynamic analysis, techno-economic assessment, life cycle assessment, and digital twin or AI integration-rather than addressing them in isolation. As such, single-dimension assessment dominates the field, with thermodynamic modelling, techno-economic assessment, and life cycle assessment each addressed independently in 67.6%, 53.9%, and 47.1% of reviewed studies respectively, while only 31.4% incorporate digital twin or AI components. These disciplinary silos are also driving assessment inconsistency, with methodological choices alone generating cost variation of up to 133% for physically identical production systems. However, the integrated frameworks that do exist have remained consistently superior in decision-making quality, with the 13 fully integrated studies producing qualitatively different technology rankings and cost-parity thresholds compared to single-dimension analyses. Integrated assessment can mitigate the risk of misallocated investment and policy error, although there are concerns about the disconnect between operational optimisation and lifecycle consequences, and the absence of standardised cross-dimensional costing protocols. Indeed, approximately 87.3% of economic studies ignore exergy destruction costs and 95.8% of life cycle assessments rely on static rather than dynamic inventories. Future integrated assessment frameworks must account for factors such as real-time dynamic life cycle inventory updating, standardised exergoeconomic costing, equity dimensions, and empirical validation of multi-year predictions.

title: Wood-based hydrogels for wearable sensors: From multi-level structure design to machine learning-enabled applications
abstract: Wood, as a natural and renewable resource, possesses a unique hierarchical porous structure and chemical components consisting of cellulose, hemicellulose, and lignin. Through physical, chemical, or biological methods such as lignin removal, component separation, or in-situ modification of wood, it can be transformed into advanced material platforms with multi-scale structural design. This article systematically reviews the preparation strategies, performance characteristics, and application progress of wood-based hydrogels. By using two main technical paths of “top-down” lignin removal to retain the natural framework and “bottom-up” component separation and reconstruction, wood-based hydrogels with excellent mechanical properties and tunable functions have been successfully developed. These materials show great potential in flexible sensing, biomedical, and energy storage fields. The introduction of artificial intelligence technologies, such as machine learning, is promoting the transformation of material research from empirical trial-and-error to data-driven rational design. However, this field still faces challenges such as the difficulty in balancing component separation efficiency and scale-up costs, and the unclear relationship between complex structures and their macroscopic properties. Future research should focus on green and efficient component separation technologies, deepening the understanding of multi-scale structure-performance relationships, and actively expanding their applications in emerging fields such as wearable sensors and sustainable flexible electronics.

title: Artificial intelligence for geological CO2 storage: From surrogate prediction to uncertainty-aware decision making
abstract: Geological CO2 storage (GCS) is a key technology for achieving net-zero emissions; however, its gigatonne-scale deployment remains constrained by the difficulty of accurately predicting subsurface CO2 migration and rigorously quantifying associated uncertainty and risk. Although physics-based numerical simulators provide high-fidelity representations of coupled multiphase flow processes, their substantial computational cost severely limits ensemble-based uncertainty quantification (UQ) and decision-oriented analyses. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have enabled a new generation of surrogate modeling frameworks that are transforming GCS from simulation-based prediction to risk-informed lifecycle management. This review provides a critical synthesis of this evolution, proposing a unified framework that bridges algorithmic advances with engineering decision-making. We trace the evolution of AI surrogates in GCS, from classical statistical surrogates and grid-dependent deep learning models to physics-informed frameworks and resolution-invariant neural operators, critically assessing their strengths and limitations for long-horizon subsurface CO2 plume migration forecasting. Furthermore, our analysis of AI-driven UQ in GCS focuses on generative geological modeling for characterizing aleatoric uncertainty and Bayesian frameworks for quantifying epistemic uncertainty, with particular emphasis on their limitations and scalability. Crucially, we extend this analysis to closed-loop decision frameworks and highlight that the main challenge in field-scale deployment lies in bridging the simulation-to-reality gap. This requires continuous data assimilation and uncertainty-aware digital rehearsal. Finally, we identify key challenges and provide a strategic roadmap toward next-generation intelligent GCS ecosystems. Central to this roadmap is an integrated lifecycle framework linking prediction, UQ, and operational decision-making, providing a pathway toward scalable, trustworthy, and adaptive GCS management.

title: Can renewable energy meet the surging power demand of artificial intelligence? A systematic review
abstract: Whether renewable energy can scale fast enough to meet the surging power demand of artificial intelligence (AI) without undermining broader decarbonization goals is the central question of this review. A PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic review of 88 peer-reviewed studies (2019–2025; Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore) yields four findings. First, peer-reviewed per-task inference energy spans more than three orders of magnitude, with image generation at approximately 1450 times a text-classification baseline and video generation substantially higher per frame; reasoning and agentic AI are an emerging modality with no peer-reviewed end-to-end measurements as of the search date. Second, corporate procurement instruments resolve into four tiers—unbundled RECs, physical PPAs, project-anchoring VPPAs, and 24/7 hourly-matched carbon-free energy—and the binding “additionality gap” lies between the lowest and highest tier. Third, four actionable pathways are identified: carbon-aware scheduling, long-duration energy storage, AI-optimized grid management, and optimal data center siting under joint grid-carbon, renewable-resource, cooling-climate, and network-latency constraints. Fourth, institutional differences across the United States, China, the European Union, and the Republic of Korea make one-size-fits-all disclosure and matching mandates unlikely to be effective. The IEA’s April 2025 Energy and AI report projects a Base Case global data center demand of approximately 945 TWh by 2030—comparable to Japan’s annual electricity consumption—rising to approximately 1200 TWh by 2035. Renewable energy can meet AI-driven demand in principle, but only conditional on accelerated deployment, a procurement shift from annual to hourly matching, and jurisdiction-matched policy frameworks for transparent energy reporting.

title: Advances in machine learning for biomass pyrolysis: Product prediction, process optimization and mechanistic interpretation
abstract: Biomass pyrolysis has attracted significant attention because of its ability to simultaneously produce fuels and value-added chemicals. However, both conventional and advanced pyrolysis methods still exhibit limited predictive accuracy and applicability. In addition, biomass pyrolysis involves complex reaction pathways, and product distributions are influenced by multiple factors, including feedstock properties, reaction conditions, and catalysts. With the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML) has emerged as a promising tool for biomass pyrolysis research. By establishing non-linear relationships between inputs and outputs, ML has demonstrated strong potential for product prediction, process optimization, and reaction mechanism interpretation. This review summarizes recent progress in the application of ML for predicting multiple pyrolysis products, including biochar, bio-oil and syngas. It also discusses the integration of optimization algorithms, such as genetic algorithms (GA), particle swarm optimization (PSO), and bayesian optimization algorithms (BOA), for process optimization and inverse design. Furthermore, the integrated application of ML with explainable AI (XAI), physical constrained models, and advanced representation techniques has shown unique advantage in elucidating reaction mechanisms and characterizing feedstock structures. In addition, this review highlights the potential of ML in sustainability assessment through its integration with life cycle assessment (LCA) and techno-economic analysis (TEA). Finally, key challenges and future research directions are discussed to support the development of reliable, efficient, and sustainable ML-assisted biomass pyrolysis systems.

title: Machine learning-assisted design and optimization of thermoacoustic devices: Progress and perspectives
abstract: Thermoacoustic technology plays an important role in the development of renewable energy. Owing to its simple structure, reliable operation, and environmental friendliness, it has been widely applied in energy-related fields such as refrigeration, power generation, and waste heat recovery. However, the performance of thermoacoustic systems highly depends on the coordinated matching among multiple components, and the design and optimization process is characterized by strong nonlinearity and multi-parameter coupling, making traditional methods inefficient. With the development of artificial intelligence (AI), data-driven modeling and global optimization capabilities have gradually promoted research progress in performance improvement and parameter optimization of thermoacoustic devices. Therefore, this paper focuses on thermoacoustic engines (TAEs), thermoacoustic refrigerators (TARs), and their key components, and systematically reviews the current applications and future prospects of machine learning in performance prediction, parameter optimization, and design optimization. This paper aims to help readers comprehensively understand the development trends of machine learning-assisted thermoacoustic research and provide references for its engineering applications and technological innovation in the field of green energy utilization.

title: Towards smart thermal energy management: A review on machine learning for control and optimization of active phase change systems in buildings
abstract: The building sector constitutes a substantial share of global energy consumption and carbon emissions, highlighting the critical need for the development of near-zero energy buildings and smart energy systems. Active phase change material (PCM) systems incorporate dynamic components to facilitate on-demand control of PCM energy storage and release processes, significantly improving the thermal management capabilities and energy scheduling flexibility of building envelopes. However, these systems exhibit complex characteristics, including multivariable interactions, strong nonlinearity, and time-varying behaviors. These complexities pose significant challenges for traditional physics-based modeling and rule-based control methods in achieving real-time optimization and global decision-making. Consequently, such methods often encounter issues like high computational costs, limited accuracy, and inadequate adaptability. Recently, the advent of machine learning technologies has introduced a novel, data-driven paradigm to address these challenges. This review systematically examines research on machine learning applications for controlling and optimizing active PCM systems in buildings. Initially, it explores research advancements and key design parameters for active PCM systems integrated into walls, floors, and ceilings. Subsequently, it critically evaluates the limitations of traditional methods while detailing the opportunities and breakthrough applications enabled by machine learning, including efficient alternate modeling, intelligent control, and multi-objective parameter optimization. Finally, it provides a comprehensive discussion of current research, highlights major challenges such as data dependence, model interpretability, and real-time deployment, and outlines future research directions. The aim of this work is to promote the deep integration of machine learning, building physics, and energy systems engineering, offering valuable insights for the development of next-generation intelligent, adaptive, and low-carbon building energy systems.

title: Data driven reveals the upgrading mechanism of waste PET electrolysis: Research progress of machine learning in collaborative production of high-value chemicals and green hydrogen energy
abstract: The pollution of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) plastics poses a global environmental challenge, and traditional recycling technologies are limited by downgrading cycles and high energy consumption. Electrocatalytic upgrading recycling can convert waste PET into high-value chemicals and synergistically produce hydrogen under mild conditions, but its multi-step electron/proton transfer, competitive reaction pathway, and complex catalyst structure-activity relationship make it difficult to efficiently break through traditional trial and error methods. Machine learning (ML), as a data-driven new paradigm, provides systematic solutions for rational catalyst design, deep mechanism analysis, and multi-objective system optimization by integrating multi-source data, constructing quantitative structure-activity relationships, analyzing reaction networks, and intelligently navigating parameter spaces. This review is the first to construct a full chain methodological framework of data algorithm application, systematically reviewing the latest progress of ML in the field of PET electrolysis collaborative production of high-value chemicals and green hydrogen energy, and looking forward to cutting-edge directions such as independent experiments, generative AI, and multimodal fusion, aiming to provide theoretical guidance for the technological development and knowledge system construction in this field.

title: Evolution of honey authentication and traceability: From conventional assays to intelligent systems integrating multi-omics and machine/deep learning for sustainable apiculture
abstract: BackgroundHoney authentication and traceability are paramount for ensuring product integrity and consumer trust within the global apiculture industry. Authentication focuses on detecting deliberate fraud, such as syrup adulteration, water dilution, and inferior honey blending, which directly undermines product quality and safety. In contrast, traceability aims to verify and confirm the declared botanical, geographical, and entomological origins of honey, which is essential for quality differentiation, protected designation, and supply chain transparency. The limitations of conventional single-dimensional analytical techniques, such as melissopalynology and isotope ratio mass spectrometry, in addressing increasingly sophisticated fraud and complex verification needs necessitate more robust, integrated solutions.

title: Harnessing artificial intelligence to engineer phage-derived enzymes for next-generation food safety
abstract: BackgroundPhage-derived enzymes (PDEs), comprising endolysins, depolymerases, and membrane-active holins/spanins, have emerged as promising biocontrol agents for food safety. Characterized by high target specificity, inherent biocompatibility, and low resistance propensity, PDEs offer a sustainable response to the converging pressures of antimicrobial resistance and consumer demand for “clean label” products. However, industrial translation remains stalled in the “Valley of Death” due to intrinsic constraints: narrow host spectra, compounded by the gram-negative outer membrane barrier, and limited stability under food processing conditions. Empirical “Engineering 1.0” strategies, including chimeragenesis, surface charge remodeling, domain truncation, and Artilysin fusion, have reached a combinatorial ceiling, where the simultaneous optimization of multiple traits exceeds the capacity of traditional trial-and-error approaches.

title: In-situ 3D visualization of high-temperature damage of ceramifiable FRP composites under compressive loading using X-ray tomography and deep learning
abstract: Ceramifiable FRP composites have attracted considerable attention due to their exceptional properties and extensive potential applications as thermal protection materials. However, the service temperature significantly affects their mechanical properties and failure behaviors. To date, systematic studies on the internal damage evolution and failure mechanisms of ceramifiable FRP composites under mechanical loading at elevated temperatures are lacking. In this study, in-situ synchrotron X-ray computed tomography (XCT) is used to obtain the 3D morphology evolution of ceramifiable FRP composites under compressive loading from room temperature to 1000 °C for the first time. The internal damage was classified into four kinds (including warp-weft fiber debonding, matrix crack, interfiber failure, and delamination), and identified by a convolutional neuronal network model. At the same time, a detailed and in-depth study was conducted on the internal damage evolution of these four kinds of cracks with the changes in load levels and temperatures. It is found that the main damage types and degrees are highly correlated with temperature. Additionally, the evolution of 3D strain was calculated by digital volume correlation technology, and the correlation between the high-strain region and the fracture location was analyzed. This study provides a new and practical way to quantitatively analyze and automatically track the micro-crack evolution behavior inside ceramifiable composites in 3D view.

title: Model distillation driven machine learning for automatic microstructure detection and segmentation
abstract: Microstructure, the internal arrangement of a material’s components, is a key determinant of its performance. Accurate microstructure analysis is essential for understanding material properties and identifying defects. Traditional manual methods are often time-consuming, while current machine learning models for microstructure segmentation require extensive labeled data and often struggle to generalize across different materials. To address these challenges, we propose the Self-annotated and Distilled U-Net (SDU-Net) framework, a versatile approach for microstructure segmentation that doesn’t require pre-existing labeled data. SDU-Net utilizes the Segment Anything Model (SAM) as a teacher model to generate initial pseudo labels for microstructure image elements through a two-step clustering process. These labels are then refined, enabling SDU-Net to learn general features and handle tasks with well-defined labels. Model distillation and preprocessing techniques within SDU-Net provide high-quality pseudo labels that guide and accelerate the training of a U-Net student model. This approach overcomes the data specificity limitations of the teacher model, significantly improving both accuracy and inference speed. By delivering precise and efficient segmentation across diverse microstructure tasks, SDU-Net offers a new paradigm for using foundation model distillation in image segmentation and demonstrates immense potential for advancing material characterization and personalized microstructural analysis.

title: Machine learning-assisted prediction and optimization of electrocatalytic activity
abstract: Electrocatalysts play a pivotal role in advancing sustainable development, fostering the generation of clean energy, mitigating global warming, and offering solutions to environmental challenges. The anticipation of catalytic activity and the optimization of electrocatalysts emerge as crucial tasks. Machine learning (ML) is rapidly emerging as a potent tool for establishing quantitative structure-activity relationships, expediting the exploration of electrocatalysis by extracting insights from historical data and refining the design of electrocatalysts. This review provides a comprehensive introduction and an in-depth review of ML techniques employed in electrocatalysis research. This paper discusses the challenges in the fields of hydrogen evolution reaction, oxygen evolution reaction, oxygen reduction reaction, carbon dioxide reduction reaction and nitrogen reduction reaction, and shows the progress of ML application in these fields. Illustrative examples are provided to demonstrate how ML models can optimize electrocatalysts and elucidate electrocatalytic reaction mechanisms. The document consolidates prevailing ML techniques, offering material scientists methods to predict and optimize electrocatalytic activity. Recognizing the tremendous potential of ML in electrocatalytic science research, it proves instrumental in predicting and optimizing efficient electrocatalytic activity reactions.

Recognizing the tremendous potential of ML in electrocatalytic science research, it proves instrumental in predicting and optimizing efficient electrocatalytic activity reactions.

title: Geometric feature-based machine learning-assisted exploration of ort-M2B2 structures for room-temperature hydrogen storage
abstract: The quest for efficient and stable solid-state hydrogen storage materials at room temperature remains a formidable challenge. This work presents a machine learning (ML)-guided framework to systematically evaluate the hydrogen storage performance of orthorhombic MBene (ort-MBene) materials. A comprehensive set of 18 ort-MBenes was investigated using density functional theory (DFT), revealing a strong correlation between their geometric characteristics and the charge transfer of the transition metals. Through this integrated ML-DFT approach, five promising MBene structures—Ti2B2, Cr2B2, Mn2B2, Zr2B2, and Hf2B2—were identified, exhibiting exceptional hydrogen adsorption capacities with preferential adsorption occurring at two bridge sites. The analysis of feature importance and Shapley additive explanations revealed that structural parameters such as the ratio of lattice constants (b/a) and the length of bonds (ΔL) were critical in determining adsorption stability, accounting for 71% of the variance in adsorption energy (Eav). Crucially, Ti2B2 demonstrates room-temperature viability: AIMD simulations confirm rapid hydrogen release (3.27 wt% within 0.5 ps) at 300–400 K. The results show that this ML-DFT framework can effectively accelerate the discovery of novel hydrogen storage materials, advance the fundamental design principles of MBene-based hydrogen adsorption materials, and serve as a valuable tool for future developments in the field of solid-state hydrogen storage.

title: Achieving superior corrosion resistance in HVAF-sprayed Fe-based amorphous alloy coatings through data-driven machine learning
abstract: Amorphous alloy coatings are emerging as very promising corrosion-resistant materials for surface engineering applications and their corrosion resistance is greatly sensitive to porosity feature, which is dependent upon the process parameters during thermal spraying. However, the preparation of high-quality thermally sprayed coatings with controlled porosity has been an ever-present challenge. In this paper, based on high-throughput preparation, a self-built dataset containing 336 coating samples was established for machine learning algorithm optimization to obtain Fe-based amorphous coatings with low porosity and high corrosion resistance. Three advanced automated machine learning algorithms: AutoGluon, FLAML, and TPOT, were employed to identify the intricate relationship between high-dimensional process parameters and the two target properties. Accordingly, two high-quality prediction models for porosity and corrosion day were developed with R² values of 0.91 and 0.98, respectively. Further, based on a well-trained porosity model, an interpolation space containing 11,039 spraying process parameters was created. The optimal coatings predicted in this parameter space achieve less than 0.5% porosity and exhibit excellent long-term corrosion resistance, including stable high-impedance modulus values over 50 days and no rusting after 100 days of immersion testing. Additionally, the attainment of optimal coatings is attributed to the reduction of splattering during deposition and higher than 75% proportion of disk-like splats. This research strategy enables the controlled preparation of thermal spray coatings with different porosities and provides innovative ideas for the efficient and reliable preparation of high-performance thermal spray coatings.

title: Decoding viscosity-microstructure relationships in the ternary CaO-SiO2-Fe O system via integrated machine learning and multimodal characterization
abstract: This study investigates the viscosity and microstructure of the ternary CaO-SiO2-FexO system using a combination of deep neural network (DNN) learning, in-situ Raman spectroscopy, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and quantum chemical ab initio calculation. A DNN-based viscosity prediction model was developed using a dataset of 1483 experimental data points, which were partitioned into training, validation, and test sets at a 5:2:3 ratio for model training and evaluation. The model achieved high prediction accuracy with a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.9464 and a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.069. The dataset encompasses the key compositional range of metallurgical slags, spanning 0–70 mol % SiO2, 0–70 mol % CaO, and 0–90 mol % FexO. The model enables rapid and accurate viscosity predictions, reducing the need for extensive experimental measurements. Microstructure analysis via XPS and Raman spectroscopy revealed that with increasing iron content, the silicon-oxygen tetrahedron (SiOT) network structure is disrupted, leading to a transformation from Si–O–Si to Si–O–Fe and Fe–O–Fe bonds, accompanied by a decrease in viscosity. This study also quantitatively correlates the Fe3+/(Fe3++Si4+) ratio in tetrahedral coordination with melt viscosity through structure descriptors (NBO/Si ratio). These results demonstrate that an increase in the tetrahedral Fe3+/(Fe3++Si4+) ratio nonlinearly elevates NBO/Si values (correlation coefficient r = 0.99), which linearly reduces melt viscosity (r = 0.96) through depolymerization of the SiOT network. The established model provides a predictive framework for viscosity optimization in metallurgical slag design and quantitative analysis of magma transport dynamics in geological systems.

title: Predicting mechanical properties of as-rolled eutectic Mg-8Li alloy via machine learning
abstract: In order to elucidate the intricate, non-linear association between rolling process parameters and the mechanical properties of the eutectic Mg-8Li alloy, this work proposes a predictive framework that integrates machine learning and explainable analysis. A “rolling parameter-mechanical property” dataset constructed from experimental data is used to develop prediction models for ultimate tensile strength (UTS), yield strength (YS), and elongation (EL) based on six machine learning algorithms: support vector regression (SVR), random forest (RF), XGBoost, AdaBoost, extra trees, and CatBoost, with the Bayesian optimization framework and cross-validation strategy employed to enhance model generalization. The results indicate that the random forest model exhibits the best performance for UTS prediction (coefficient of determination R2 = 0.9452, mean absolute error MAE = 2.07), the SVR model achieves the highest accuracy for YS prediction (R2 = 0.9524, MAE = 3.38), and the AdaBoost model demonstrates the best performance for EL prediction (R2 = 0.8676, MAE = 1.65). Additionally, by using the Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) along with the Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) method, it is shown that the initial thickness negatively affects UTS and YS, while the reduction ratio positively impacts UTS and YS the most, and the rolling temperature has a complex negative effect on EL. Experimental validation confirms the strong generalization ability and engineering applicability of the optimal models. This work clarifies the synergistic mechanism of rolling parameters through a data-driven approach, providing theoretical support and technical pathways for achieving an intelligent rolling process design for the eutectic Mg-8Li alloy.

title: Achieving interpretable and efficient design of lightweight multi-principal element alloys via machine learning with optimized strengthening-toughening models
abstract: Body-centered cubic multi-principal element alloys (BCC MPEAs) face inherent strength-ductility trade-offs. Given their vast compositional space, identifying key factors governing strength and ductility, as well as developing novel strengthening-toughening models to accelerate the property-oriented design, remains an outstanding challenge. Here, we developed an interpretable machine learning (ML) framework for BCC MPEAs to identify the key factors governing yield strength (YS) and fracture elongation (FE). The results demonstrate that FE mainly arises from the synergistic effects of multiple factors (electronegativity difference Δχpauling, valence electron concentration VEC, and density ρ), while average shear modulus mismatch δGave is the dominant factor controlling YS. Using these screened features as inputs, we propose optimized YS and FE models that achieve high predictive accuracy (YS: R2=0.96, FE: R2=0.84) and outperform existing models. By transforming these ML insights into strengthening/toughening theories via feature-to-mechanical performance/element property mapping, we designed three novel Ti-Zr-based BCC MPEAs with exceptional properties: YS of 1.07–1.16 GPa, FE of 16.6 %–24.5 %, and specific yield strength of ∼170 MPa cm3 g−1, surpassing most reported BCC MPEAs. This work not only provides a data-driven strategy to overcome the strength-ductility trade-off in BCC MPEAs but also establishes interpretable design principles for accelerating the discovery of advanced structural materials.

title: Exploring the erosion-corrosion behavior of copper-nickel alloys via machine learning
abstract: This study proposes a physics-informed machine learning framework to predict the erosion-corrosion behavior of copper-nickel alloys in seawater environments. A dataset comprising 857 samples with 13 features was evaluated using nine different machine learning algorithms. Among these, AdaBoost and CatBoost demonstrated the highest predictive accuracy for the non-immersion and immersion conditions, respectively. SHAP value analysis identified alloy composition, flow velocity, and immersion history as the most influential factors. Based on the optimized model, an extended dataset consisting of 70,000 samples was generated and analyzed. The effects of various environmental factors on the corrosion behavior of 90/10 and 70/30 copper-nickel alloys were investigated. This analysis revealed the key influencing factors governing the corrosion behavior of copper-nickel alloys, and the critical flow velocities of 90/10 and 70/30 copper-nickel alloys were thus derived. This research enhances predictive reliability and provides mechanistic insights, offering valuable guidance for alloy design, seawater system operation, and maintenance strategies.

title: Ultrasensitive CSF rhinorrhea screening via machine learning-aided SERS on Au@Ag nanopillars
abstract: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) rhinorrhea often presents as clear nasal discharge, making it challenging to differentiate from normal secretions and delaying diagnosis. As CSF leakage provides a direct pathway for pathogen entry into the central nervous system, rapid and accurate detection is essential to prevent severe infections such as meningitis. This study introduces a machine learning (ML)-assisted surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) diagnostic platform that reliably distinguishes CSF from nasal secretion samples. The core sensing element is an Au@Ag bimetallic nanopillar substrate, engineered to exploit synergistic plasmonic effects between gold and silver for maximal SERS enhancement while offering superior corrosion resistance. This high-performance substrate enables sensitive and reproducible detection of clinical specimens. To address spectral resolution and range inconsistencies among different Raman instruments, a cross-instrument spectral preprocessing algorithm was developed to standardize input spectra. Among the ML pipelines evaluated, the NearMiss-2 (NM2)-logistic regression (LR) model demonstrated the highest classification performance in both internal and external validations. Notably, when applied to spectra from a portable Raman spectrometer, the NM2-LR pipeline achieved a 0.95 true positive rate and a 1.00 true negative rate. This Au@Ag nanopillar-based ML-SERS platform provides a rapid, cost-effective, and portable solution for CSF rhinorrhea diagnosis, with significant potential for broader biomedical applications.

title: Revealing loss mechanisms through interpretable machine learning and accelerated discovery of ultra-low-loss dielectric ceramics in the Li2TiO3-Li3NbO4-MgO system
abstract: The optimization of ultra-low-loss microwave dielectric ceramics is hindered by the complex interplay of factors governing the dielectric loss and inefficient trial-and-error screening. This study introduces an interpretable machine learning framework that combines accelerated materials discovery with quantitative structure-property analysis for the Li2TiO3-Li3NbO4-MgO system. A Gaussian process regression-based active learning strategy was employed to explore the compositional space, identifying the near-optimal composition of (1−x)Li3MgNbO5-xLi2TiO3 at x = 0.80 using only six compositions (from a total of 21) over three iterations, closely aligning with the experimentally determined optimum at x = 0.85. Beyond optimization, a high-fidelity ensemble machine learning model (R2 = 0.8285) was developed to quantitatively evaluate the influence of twelve physically meaningful structural descriptors on dielectric loss, utilizing permutation importance and SHapley Additive exPlanations. Both methods consistently identified internal strain (IS) and configurational entropy (CE) as the most dominant factors influencing Q × f. Maximum Q × f value arises from a synergistic combination of moderate CE associated with order-disorder transitions, minimized IS, and a densely packed microstructure with elevated relative density. Experimental and model validation confirms that the composition at x = 0.85 achieves outstanding dielectric performance, with εr = 16.17, Q × f = 104,300 GHz at 9.2 GHz, and τf = −3.47 ppm/°C. This closed-loop, interpretable, and experimentally supported methodology offers a generalizable route for the rapid design of high-performance dielectric ceramics.

title: A machine learning strategy to achieve strength-conductivity-ductility synergy of high‐performance Cu-Ni-Co-Si alloys via rolling and aging process
abstract: The alloying elements and rolling/aging parameters have a critical influence on the microstructure and properties of precipitation-strengthened Cu-Ni-Co-Si alloys. Nevertheless, the complexity of alloy composition, variability in processing parameters, and conflicting relationships among material properties impede the concurrent improvement of overall performance characteristics. To address this, we developed a machine learning design strategy and explored the complex effects of key features through feature engineering and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis. Subsequently, the NSGA-II algorithm was used to optimize alloy composition, and a multi-step rolling and aging process was developed to further tailor microstructure and performance. The results demonstrate that the alloy exhibits exceptional properties after multi-step rolling and aging. The new alloy achieves ultimate tensile strength, electrical conductivity, and elongation of the values of 911.4 MPa, 44.37 % IACS, and 7.3 %, respectively. The remarkable properties of Cu-Ni-Co-Si-Mg-Ti alloys are primarily ascribed to the retention of specific crystallographic textures, notably Brass and S, alongside the precipitation of alloying elements such as Ni, Co, and Si. Preserving these cold-rolled textures is crucial for maintaining high strength. title: Interpretable high-throughput machine learning-based screening of high-thermal-conductivity composites with experimental validation
abstract: With the rapid development of electronic devices, energy storage systems, and aerospace technologies, the demand for polymer-based composites with high thermal conductivity (TC) has become increasingly urgent. However, traditional trial-and-error research approaches heavily depended on individual research experience, and extensive experimental validation often fails to reveal the complex relationships between composite formulations and thermal performances. Herein, an efficient machine learning (ML)-based framework for screening composites with high TC was proposed, aiming to optimize the material design process, reduce experimental costs, and identify the key factors influencing TC. Firstly, a comprehensive dataset comprising 370 valid samples is constructed from published literature for thermally conductive carbon-filled/polymer composites. Subsequently, two hybrid models of Logistic+XGBoost and Logistic+fully connected neural network (FCNN) (LFCNN) are developed via a residual-corrected strategy by integrating Logistic regression with XGBoost or a FCNN to improve the capacity of capturing both linear and nonlinear features. Noticeably, LFCNN exhibits the best performance with a classification accuracy of 96.77%. Quantitative analysis using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) reveals that numerical features exhibit significantly higher importance than categorical features, with filler loading identified as the dominant factor. Within a high-throughput designed compositional space of 32327 sample groups, three promising candidates were selected using LFCNN and experimental validation, where the measured TC is fully consistent with the model predictions. This ML-based framework demonstrates the great promise of integrating ML with experimental validation to accelerate the development of high-thermal-conductivity polymer-based composites and provides new insights into the interpretable application of ML in materials science.

title: Interpretable machine learning for predicting tensile twinning and revealing microstructural influences in pure Mg
abstract: Tensile twinning plays a pivotal role in the plastic deformation of Mg alloys, and its nucleation is governed by the coupling of multiple microstructural factors. Focusing on pure Mg, we combine electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) with machine learning to develop a predictive model that captures multivariate interactions controlling tensile twinning. Thirty-four microstructural descriptors were extracted, an Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) classifier was trained on 5669 grains strained to 1%, and the model was interpreted using Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP). In addition to the Schmid factor (SF) for tensile twinning, the analysis reveals that grain size, the SF for slip, grain morphology, and neighboring grain attributes significantly influence tensile twin nucleation. Tensile twinning is favored in large, irregularly shaped grains and in grains located within neighborhoods that provide poor strain accommodation. Moreover, tensile twinning in low SF grains is not anomalous and can be attributed to the inability of strain accommodation to sufficiently release the local stress, leading to its accumulation near complex grain boundaries and thereby facilitating twin nucleation. External validation on AZ31 and GW93 alloys confirms strong predictive performance and transferability across distinct Mg alloy systems. This study provides data-driven insight into the nucleation of tensile twin in Mg alloys and establishes a practical framework for microstructure design and deformation control in the development of high-performance Mg alloys.

title: Coupled damage evolution of Cf/SiC composites across a full oxygen concentration gradient at elevated temperature via synchrotron in-situ CT and deep learning
abstract: To elucidate the effect of environmental oxygen concentration on damage evolution in Cf/SiC composites at high temperature, an integrated platform incorporating ultrahigh‑temperature in‑situ loading with synchrotron‑radiation µCT (SR‑µCT) was constructed. This platform enabled real‑time observation of coupled thermo‑mechanical‑oxidative damage in Cf/SiC at 1400 °C under 0, 0.5 vol.%, 5 vol.%, and 21 vol.% O2. Combined with the nnU‑Net deep‑learning framework, the 3D evolution of coating cracks, voids, oxidation damage, and delamination was visualised and quantified. Integrating SR‑µCT with fractography elucidated the sequential evolution from damage initiation to final failure. Tensile strength decreased with increasing oxygen concentration. Under inert conditions, coating cracks propagated periodically with continuous nucleation, void morphology remained stable, and failure was abrupt and brittle. At O2 ≥ 0.5 vol.%, oxidation‑induced damage initially propagated along pre‑existing coating cracks; fibres in the crack‑contact zone were oxidised first, and damage extended along the fibre orientation, resulting in a 3D damage field aligned with the crack path. At O2 ≥ 5 vol.%, oxidation induced new microvoids whose growth and coalescence increased void volume and formed a 3D network. Collectively, these processes established a cycle where voids accelerated oxygen diffusion, accelerated diffusion induced further damage, and damage produced more voids. This work provides an effective four-dimensional analysis method for investigating the coupled evolution of multiple damage modes in ceramic-matrix composites under high-temperature oxidation.

title: Controlled pore evolution in liquid precursor-derived ceramic matrix composites driven by deep learning-assisted XCT analysis
abstract: In-depth insights into the high residual porosity in liquid precursor-derived ceramic matrix composites (CMCs) have long been elusive, constrained by the limited spatial characterization techniques. In this study, systematic deep learning-assisted X-ray micro-computed tomography tracking revealed that a competitive pore-filling mechanism in the traditional liquid-precursor route fundamentally impeded the further densification of a SiC fiber-woven CMC. An innovative strategy combining in-situ curing with capillary pressure-induced self-aggregation was proposed, enabling dynamic regulation of precursor-derived matrix for synergistic filling of multiscale pores. Consequently, the porosity of SiCf-CMC was reduced from 18.6% to 6.2%, reaching a level significantly lower than that of comparable CMCs, accompanied by a notable increase in flexural strength from 68.1 to 220.7 MPa. Moreover, the resulting composite retained over 90% of the strength after water-oxygen exposures at 1200–1400 °C for 5 h. This work provides new insights into pore regulation of CMCs for advanced aerospace thermal structural applications.

title: Energy-efficient, high-accuracy sensing in loose-fitting textile sensor matrix for LLM-enabled human-robot collaboration
abstract: Textile-based sensing systems hold significant promise for wearable human–robot interfaces, but many existing approaches lack one or more key attributes, such as pixel-level self-powering, high spatial resolution, or the ability to balance wearing comfort with sensing accuracy and reliability. Furthermore, few solutions demonstrate adaptability across physical platforms or integration with semantic reasoning frameworks. Here, we present a multifunctional textile sensor matrix (TSM) that addresses these limitations by combining woven Schottky-diode junctions for localized self-powered sensing, deep learning (DL) for denoising and feature extraction, and large language model (LLM) integration for high-level task planning. Each pixel, approximately 300 µm × 400 µm in size, provides dual-mode output for pressure sensing and energy harvesting, achieving 75 mV kPa−1 voltage sensitivity, 0.82 nA kPa−1 current sensitivity, and 14 µW cm−2 power output. Each sensing pixel measures ∼300 µm × 400 µm, with an achieved density of ∼48 cm−2. The system achieves 98.22 % accuracy in gesture recognition, 97.02 % in object identification, and 94.03 % in robotic hand adaptation via transfer learning. Beyond perception, integration with LLM supports high-level task planning, establishing a tactile-language-action (TLA) framework. This work introduces a scalable, energy-efficient, and cognitively integrated textile platform for adaptive human–robot collaboration and embodied AI.

title: Self-powered heart real-time monitoring system based on triboelectric and piezoelectric hybrid nanogenerator and artificial intelligence technology
abstract: By converting biomechanical energy from human walking into electrical energy, the triboelectric and piezoelectric hybrid nanogenerator (TPHG) can immediately and sustainably power the heart rate monitoring system. The designed system displays a swift runtime of 14 ms and low energy consumption at 220 μJ. The acquired electrocardiogram (ECG) signals can be transferred by a wireless module to an artificial intelligence (AI) cloud server and displayed on a smartphone or personal computer in real time. This work paves the key way for designing self-powered real-time monitoring systems.

title: Spatiotemporal decoding of laryngeal motion using flexible triboelectric arrays and deep learning assistance
abstract: The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has driven innovations in human-machine interaction through tightly coupled perception systems. Electronic skins (e-skins) are a crucial technology for developing these perceptive capabilities. However, existing e-skins face challenges such as reliance on external power, complex fabrication, and signal processing sophistication. Here, we introduce a screen-printed triboelectric sensor array (TSA) integrated with a two-dimensional convolutional neural network (2D-CNN) for high-fidelity laryngeal motion decoding, to establish an intelligent laryngeal muscle decoding system. The conductive silver paste with exceptional electrical conductivity (0.23 Ω/sq) function as electrode in the TSA, enabling high sensitivity (1.651 V/kPa), good mechanical durability and seamless epidermal integration. By harnessing the 2D-CNN's spatiotemporal feature extraction capability, the system achieves 99.6 % accuracy in classifying laryngeal movements, surpassing conventional time-series analysis methods. The proposed system enables concurrent high-spatial-resolution tactile sensing, and pressure sensing, demonstrating remarkable superiority over human tactile acuity in both resolution and sensitivity. This study presents a self-powered, flexible sensing system capable of decoding subtle laryngeal muscle motions. By integrating a deep learning model, the system effectively classifies laryngeal motion patterns associated with specific words, offering a new possibility for the exploration of speech rehabilitation and next-generation wearable human-computer interaction.

title: Advances in machine learning (ML)-driven design of two-dimensional materials for energy and environmental applications
abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) materials, with atomic-scale thickness, tunable electronic structures, and complex interfacial chemistry, are attracting increasing attention for sustainable energy conversion and environmental remediation. However, conventional experimental and first-principles screening methods remain slow and costly, restricting exploration of their vast compositional and structural diversity. This review summarizes recent progress in machine learning (ML)-assisted design of 2D materials, highlighting commonly applied supervised, unsupervised, and semi-supervised algorithms, feature-engineering techniques, and open databases. The integration of ML with density functional theory (DFT) accelerates the discovery of high-performance electrodes, guides the optimization of electrocatalysts and photocatalysts, and enables efficient screening of thermoelectric, sensing, desalination, and pollutant-removal systems. Emerging ML applications in toxicity evaluation and safety assessment are also discussed. Key challenges in data quality, descriptor construction, model generalization, and physical interpretability are analyzed, while future directions in physics-guided learning, automated ML, and multi-objective optimization are outlined. Overall, this review offers a comprehensive perspective that links machine learning with the rational design of 2D materials for sustainable energy and environmental systems.

title: Physics-guided machine learning for co-design of charge-pumped triboelectric nanogenerators at critical air-breakdown
abstract: Operating charge-pumped triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) at the critical air-breakdown state is essential for maximizing power output, yet it intensifies the fundamental trade-off with durability, creating a complex co-design challenge. Herein, this study first systematically investigates electromechanical mechanism in charge-pumped rotary freestanding TENG (RF-TENG) at the critical air-breakdown state. Experiments reveal that the dynamic evolution of the transfer film governs the competition between the output charge density and the wear loss, enabling establishment of the quantitative relationships among wear loss, transfer film coverage ratio and output charge density. Then, leveraging this insight, an electromechanical model is established and further a physics-guided hybrid surrogate model is constructed through integration of conditioned-modulation Gaussian process regression (CMGPR) and artificial neural network (ANN). The CMGPR-ANN framework provides efficient performance evaluation, where CMGPR enables stage-aware wear prediction while ANN captures nonlinear electrostatic induction. Ultimately, by combining this hybrid model with multi-objective optimization, the Pareto frontier between electrical performance and durability is mapped, extracting quantitative design principles for key parameters (e.g., the gap ratio) and delivering optimal designs for high-performance charge-pumped RF-TENG. This work establishes a co-design paradigm bridging physical mechanisms with computational optimization for advanced TENG development.

The CMGPR-ANN framework provides efficient performance evaluation, where CMGPR enables stage-aware wear prediction while ANN captures nonlinear electrostatic induction. Ultimately, by combining this hybrid model with multi-objective optimization, the Pareto frontier between electrical performance and durability is mapped, extracting quantitative design principles for key parameters (e.g., the gap ratio) and delivering optimal designs for high-performance charge-pumped RF-TENG. This work establishes a co-design paradigm bridging physical mechanisms with computational optimization for advanced TENG development.

title: Gradient-architected magnetic tactile skin for human-vehicle interaction: From bio-inspired design to deep learning-enabled recognition of driver operational behaviors
abstract: In the foreseeable future, human drivers will remain an indispensable role of autonomous vehicles, rendering real-time and accurate recognition of driver operational behaviors critical for driving safety and cooperative decision-making. Although flexible tactile sensors offer a promising solution for capturing driver-vehicle interactions, driver operational behaviors span a wide range of interaction forces, from subtle pre-operational cues to large-amplitude control actions, posing a significant challenge for conventional tactile sensors to achieve both high sensitivity and a broad sensing range. Inspired by the hierarchical mechanosensing mechanism of human skin, this study proposes a biomimetic gradient-structured flexible magnetic skin (BG-FMS) for fine-grained driver operational behavior recognition. The designed three-gradient elastic modulus architecture enables the BG-FMS to simultaneously provide high sensitivity to subtle operational cues and a wide dynamic range for large-amplitude driving actions, while maintaining fast response and strong environmental robustness. The BG-FMS is seamlessly integrated on the steering wheel and pedal surfaces, enabling real-time acquisition of driver operational signals. Meanwhile, a channel attention-enhanced deep learning model (CA-TCNet) is developed to accurately recognize driver operational behaviors. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed driver operational behavior recognition system achieves recognition accuracies of 99.6%, 98.0%, and 90.7% using 3 s, 2 s, and 1 s of operation data, respectively, highlighting its ultra-fast early-stage behavior recognition capability. This work presents a robust, non-intrusive, and deployable human-vehicle interaction sensing solution, thereby broadening the application scope of flexible magnetic skins in intelligent transportation and cooperative driving systems.

title: Artificial intelligence-driven paradigms for layered cathode materials: A systematic framework for multi-scale engineering
abstract: Layered cathode materials, exemplified by lithium/sodium-based layered oxides, stand at the forefront of battery research owing to their high energy density and superior ion transport characteristics. However, their design and performance optimization encounter multiscale challenges. At the atomic scale, issues include cation mixing and the unregulated oxygen redox behaviors; at the crystal scale, phase transitions and stress distributions pose significant hurdles; while at the particle scale, crack evolution and interfacial stability remain critical concerns. Traditional trial-and-error approaches are inefficient, particularly when addressing the complex interscale couplings inherent in these systems.The emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) has introduced a transformative paradigm in materials design. By synergistically integrating data-driven methodologies with fundamental physical models, AI enables cross-scale optimization—ranging from atomic defect engineering to macroscopic performance prediction. AI applications in high-throughput screening, crystal structure prediction, and dynamic process analysis have markedly accelerated the discovery and development of advanced materials. Nevertheless, critical challenges persist, including ensuring data quality and representativeness, enhancing model interpretability, and bridging the gap between computational predictions and experimental validation. This review establishes a systematic framework for evaluating AI-driven paradigms in the context of layered cathode materials, providing a multi-scale perspective that spans from atomic-level discovery to electrode-level optimization, thereby highlighting the innovative potential of AI to overcome performance bottlenecks and drive the advancement of next-generation battery technologies.

title: Bifunctional organohydrogel-based self-powered omnidirectional pressure-sensing smart ball with deep learning assistance for comprehensive hand rehabilitation assessment
abstract: Hand function rehabilitation is essential for restoring motor ability, but remains challenging due to complex biomechanics of hand, and limited omnidirectional sensing capability of existing self-powered portable devices. To overcome these challenges, we present PEDOT:PSS-doped bifunctional organohydrogel (PPBOH) based self-powered pressure-sensing stress ball (SPSB) designed for comprehensive, direction-independent monitoring of complex hand exercises. Incorporating large semiconducting polymer PEDOT: PSS into organohydrogel significantly enhanced its tribopositivity, electrical conductivity, and mechanical robustness while maintaining compressibility, resulting in two-fold increase in output voltage (621 V), and power density (1.7 W/m2). Leveraging intrinsic shape adaptability of PPBOH and facile molding approach, conical arrays were molded on PPBOH sphere, encapsulated in electronegative silicone shell, and shielded with outer PPBOH layer that effectively suppresses skin-induced triboelectric interference. The resulting SPSB exhibits superior omnidirectional sensitivity (0.453 V/N, 2.8–40 N; 0.069 V/N, 40–90 N), stability (21k cycles), mechanical compliance, and reproducibility (±6%). The SPSB was successfully employed for real-time monitoring of comprehensive hand-rehabilitation exercises and trained with deep learning model to effectively identify exercise patterns with excellent accuracy (98%). Moreover, grip strength was evaluated using s-EMG signals as reference metric that directly maps voltage and force through customized interactive rehabilitation platform. Collectively, a portable, omnidirectional pressure-sensing ball has been developed, marking substantial advance toward continuous, home-based neuromuscular rehabilitation monitoring.

title: Artificial intelligence–enabled design of a four-bar linkage triboelectric nanogenerator for wave energy harvesting
abstract: Power take-off (PTO) mechanisms are key devices that convert ocean wave energy into mechanical energy for triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs)-based wave energy converter. However, conventional PTO mechanisms, including gears and screws, are structurally complex, require high assembly precision, and are difficult to maintain, which limits their potential for large‑scale engineering applications. Moreover, the PTO mechanism parameter optimization typically depends on numerous single-variable experiments, leading to high costs and limiting the potential for globally optimal designs. Here, we propose a novel wave energy converter (WEC) whose core is a planar four‑bar linkage that converts the heaving motion of a wave‑driven buoy into the reciprocating rotation of a main shaft, and then drives the TENG rotor into unidirectional rotation via one‑way bearings for continuous electricity generation. This design not only simplifies the PTO structure but also enhances energy harvesting efficiency during both upward and downward motions. We establish a kinematic model of the PTO mechanism to predict the angular velocity of the TENG rotor, and verify the model through theoretical calculation and experimental testing of the short‑circuit current of the TENG unit. Next, we propose an AI‑assisted mechanism optimization method that uses the kinematic model to generate a dataset, combined with artificial neural network training and intelligent algorithm search, with the TENG rotor kinetic energy as the optimization objective, to optimize the mechanism parameters. This enables PTO parameters to be tailored for specific marine environments without extensive physical testing. The optimized device achieves peak and average power densities of 3.83 W/m3 and 0.746 W/m3, respectively, and after power management demonstrates the ability to power small electronic devices. This work provides a timely and cost-effective strategy for optimizing PTO mechanisms in TENG-based WECs, accelerating the transition from laboratory research to practical applications.

title: Artificial intelligence assisted self-powered water quality monitoring and early warning using a triboelectric-electromagnetic hybrid generator
abstract: Water pollution warning serves as a critical first line of defense in safeguarding public health and preserving aquatic ecosystems, especially amid growing industrial and urban pressures. However, the implementation of real-time, distributed monitoring systems along extensive pipeline networks remains hindered by formidable obstacles, including unreliable power access and limitations in real-time data analysis and predictive capacity. To address these issues, we propose a water quality sensing triboelectric and electromagnetic hybrid generator (WQS-TEHG). Via synergistic biomimetic fish-fin blade optimization and a storage-release electromagnetic generator (SR-EMG), the system harvests energy efficiently across a wide flow-velocity range. An optimized triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) sensing unit integrated with a total dissolved solids (TDS) sensor forms a multi-parameter sensing suite, its flow-sensing output frequency shows a strong linear correlation with actual flow velocity (Coefficient of determination (R²) ≈ 0.96). Building on this hardware, we develop a Temporal-Spatial convolutional network (TSCN) for early warning. By integrating spatiotemporal features from flow and TDS, the model enables the early detection of water-quality issues and delivers highly accurate parameter predictions, substantially outperforming single-input baselines (R² +0.08, RMSE −11.8). This work addresses energy constraints and limited intelligence in urban pipeline monitoring and lays the groundwork for distributed self-powered, intelligent water-monitoring networks.

title: Artificial intelligence -driven triboelectric nanogenerators for healthcare: Devices, algorithms and systems
abstract: Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) can convert biomechanical and biochemical stimuli into electrical signals without an external power source, thus enabling wearable and implantable health monitoring systems. However, triboelectric signals are sparse, nonstationary, and highly sensitive to motion, humidity, contact changes, and device aging. Their clinical value therefore depends not only on device sensitivity, but also on algorithms that transform unstable self-powered waveforms into reliable physiological information. This article reviews the intelligent TENG health-monitoring system from the perspective of the collaborative design of devices and algorithms. We first survey self-powered sensors for sweat and body-fluid analysis, pulse and blood-pressure monitoring, respiration, ocular and facial-muscle motion, implantable cardiac monitoring, and self-powered pacing. We then trace the algorithmic evolution from hand-crafted-feature machine learning to convolutional, recurrent, attention-based, multimodal, and neuromorphic models, linking each model family to the signal bottleneck it addresses. We argue that in the next stage of TENG health monitoring will no longer mainly be defined by peak output or isolated recognition accuracy, but will more reflect aspects such as calibration stability, cross-subject generalization, motion artifact suppression, energy efficiency, and clinical interpretability. Emerging architectures like state-space models and reservoir computing may provide the computational basis for low-power, real-time health systems.

title: Concurrent self-powered static-force-sensing and power-supplying triboelectric nanogenerator via electron avalanche and machine learning
abstract: With the development of artificial intelligence and internet of things sensors, global energy consumption has become a major challenge. Many researchers have aimed to develop self-powered sensors based on energy harvesting; however, these devices still generate a low-power output, which is insufficient to power an entire system. Among the various energy-harvesting technologies, triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) are promising candidates that can be easily applied to self-powered sensors. Nevertheless, TENGs have a critical limitation; although they can generate a high-voltage output, the fundamental generation mechanism inherently limits the current output to low levels. In this study, a self-powered, static-force-sensing TENG capable of functioning concurrently as a self-powered sensor and power supplier was demonstrated. Through the electrostatic discharge effect, this system generated a high electrical output via an electron avalanche during air breakdown and regulated the voltage signal through the gap distance according to Paschen's law. Consequently, this system achieved high sensing accuracy using a random forest regression model and exhibited energy-harvesting capability by powering 3000 LEDs and seven 5-W lamps and continuously operating three thermo-hygrometers.

title: Single-atom collaboration with cluster for accelerated nitrate electroreduction: Synergy revelation via machine learning and DFT calculations
abstract: Exploring high-performance electrocatalysts for the nitrate reduction reaction (NO3RR) is crucial for environmental nitrate removal and ammonia synthesis. Single-atom collaboration with cluster can provide sufficient active sites for catalysts to promote NO3RR, yet the unclear synergistic effect between the two hinders their rational design. Herein, a series of Ir3 clusters and metal single atoms co-embedded in graphitic carbon nitride (g-CN) catalysts (Ir3M1) were constructed, and the synergistic effects of Ir3 clusters and M1 single atoms on the NO3RR catalytic mechanism and activity were systematically explored using density functional theory (DFT) calculations combined with machine learning. Comprehensive evaluations of structural stability and catalytic activity demonstrate that the synergy between single atoms and clusters effectively balances the adsorption energies of key intermediates, yielding exceptional catalytic performance (the limiting potential of Ir3Ti1 can reach −0.22 V). Machine learning models further clarify the synergistic mechanism, where the geometric configurations of clusters serve as critical features for modulating the catalytic activity of single-atom sites, whereas the electronic structures of single atoms directly govern the reactivity of cluster sites. This DFT-machine learning approach provides theoretical guidelines for catalyst design and a predictive framework for efficient NO3RR electrocatalysts.

This DFT-machine learning approach provides theoretical guidelines for catalyst design and a predictive framework for efficient NO3RR electrocatalysts.

title: Machine learning-inspired process-based models for adsorption selectivity between CO2 and CH4 on coal
abstract: Adsorption selectivity of gases on porous substrates is a fundamental challenge in both materials science and applied engineering. Traditional models derived from single-component data and limited observations are insufficient to capture the integrated effects of temperature, pressure, and gas composition that govern multicomponent competitive sorption. We address this challenge by collecting then utilizing an ensemble data suite comprising 1017 entries for 43 coal samples under diverse conditions for CO2/CH4 competitive adsorption. This dataset was used to train four machine learning models to predict adsorption selectivity, among which XGBoost achieved the best performance. This ML-based model achieves a 14.6% improvement over traditional numerical models. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis was performed to investigate the individual and interaction effects of key factors on adsorption selectivity. Pressure exhibits a non-monotonic three-stage influence on selectivity, governed sequentially by energetic, entropic, and pore-network effects. Coal rank, gas composition, and pressure exhibit pronounced interactions that reshape their individual contributions. Temperature suppresses CO2 competitiveness, especially at low CO2 fractions, due to its higher adsorption heat and enhanced thermal motion. This study establishes a data-driven framework integrating ML and adsorption physics for elucidating competitive adsorption in multicomponent gas systems, thereby advancing interdisciplinary inquiry across materials science, carbon sequestration, and natural gas development.

title: Flame-retardant bimodal wrinkled strain sensor for deep learning-assisted gesture recognition and human-machine interaction
abstract: Resistive fabric-based strain sensors show great potential in wearable electronics; however, their practical applications remain limited by the intrinsic trade-off between high sensitivity and a wide strain range, as well as the inherent flammability of the fabric substrate, which poses potential safety risks under high-temperature or fire conditions. To address this issue, a flame-retardant flexible strain sensor based on a MXene/CNTs bimodal wrinkled structure was rationally designed according to a three-step procedure as follows: (i) constructing a MXene/CNTs conductive network through Ti–O–C covalent bonds, (ii) generating a bimodal wrinkled structure by swelling-deswelling-induced interfacial buckling of the thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) substrate, and (iii) integrating a biomass-derived phytic acid coating to impart flame retardancy. Benefiting from the dynamic reconfiguration of Ti–O–C bonds and the variation in wrinkles across layers during the stretching process, the sensor exhibits high sensitivity (gauge factor = 4851.23), a wide strain detection range (0%–190%), and excellent long-term stability through 10,000 cycles. Moreover, the sensor integrates passive-active fire safety, raising the membrane char residue to 40.3% at 800 °C to inhibit molten droplets and achieve self-extinguishing, while also enabling rapid high-temperature alarm triggering. As a proof-of-concept application, a wearable human-machine interaction system enables wireless gesture control and fire warning, achieving a recognition accuracy of 99.33% for five gesture commands with the assistance of deep learning. This work provides an effective strategy for integrating high-performance strain sensing with active-passive synergistic flame retardancy, offering valuable guidance for intelligent wearable electronics and safety-monitoring systems.

title: A machine learning framework for biorefinery pretreatment design
abstract: Lignocellulosic biorefineries are essential to the circular economy but are limited by biomass recalcitrance and the high cost of pretreatment optimization. Existing machine-learning approaches are typically restricted to single feedstocks or processes, largely due to fragmented and inconsistent data. Here we present LAM-Pre, a framework that integrates large language model (LLM)-assisted literature mining, systematic machine-learning benchmarking, and experimental validation to predict glucose yields across diverse pretreatment and enzymatic hydrolysis conditions. Using ChatGPT-assisted data extraction, we curated a comprehensive Pret-Glucose dataset spanning multiple biomass types, pretreatment strategies, and enzymes. Benchmarking 16 supervised models identified Gradient Boosting Decision Trees (GBDT) as the best-performing model within the current heterogeneous dataset. Experimental validation demonstrated strong trend-level consistency (up to PCC = 0.9) of glucose yields across diverse and mixed biomass feedstocks. Virtual screening of 1,092,000 process-condition combinations enabled rapid identification of high-yield regimes, including a sodium hydroxide-hydrogen peroxide pretreatment achieving 96% glucose yield. LAM-Pre was further applied to mixed biomass systems, experimentally delivering up to a 34.8% yield increase over single-feedstock processing. LAM-Pre establishes a scalable, data-driven workflow for flexible and economically viable biorefinery design.

title: Synthesis-driven discovery of high-performance fuels using ultra-high precision graph neural networks
abstract: Efforts to accelerate the development of high-performance hydrocarbon fuels with high energy density for advanced aerospace propulsion are frequently hindered by the synthetic infeasibility of designed molecules. Here, we present a molecular design framework that generates high-performance hydrocarbon fuels while explicitly defining their synthetic feedstocks and routes. Using cyclopropanation and hydrogenation reactions as templates, we design 1000 synthesizable accessibility hydrocarbons. To enable rapid and accurate property evaluation, we develop graph neural networks (GNN) models that integrate attention mechanisms and multi-order convolutional edges. These models are trained on a manually curated dataset of 2068 hydrocarbons with over 11,000 data points for density (ρ), net heat of combustion (NHOC), viscosity (η), boiling point (Tb), and melting point (Tm). The optimal models achieve prediction accuracy of 0.998, 0.997, 0.998, 0.919, and 0.996 for ρ, NHOC, Tb, Tm, and η, respectively. Predictions indicate that 174 of the designed hydrocarbons surpass the energy density of the benchmark fuel JP-10 (39.40 MJ/L), with a maximum of 46.62 MJ/L. Six of these hydrocarbons are synthesized, and the experimental values are in strong agreement with the predicted values. This result validates both the synthetic feasibility of the designed molecules and the superior predictive performance of the GNN models. This synthesis-driven design paradigm accelerates the discovery of next-generation aerospace fuels and is extendable to other small-molecule design tasks.
